Hence the Apostle elsewhere: [[Gal 5:24|And they that are Christ's have crucified their flesh, with the vices and concupiscences|Qui enim sunt Christi, carnem suam crucifixerunt cum vitiis et concupiscentiis]]. He who conforms himself to Christ crucified is fastened to his cross, and the heat of sin is quenched in him by the power of the Lord's cross; and he has his flesh pierced through with the fear of God[[Ps 118:120||]], so that his members are not stretched out to their accustomed vices.

paras.t: Vivo autem jam non ego, id est, postquam Christo confixus sum cruci, vivo et non vivo. Vivo enim non solum vita naturæ, sed gratiæ ; non vita humana, sed divina ; non vita carnali, mundana et consueta, sed spirituali, cœliformi ac nova. Ideo subditur : vivit vero in me Christus, id est, non secundum me ipsum vivo seu ago, sed secundum Christi inspirationem, voluntatem atque doctrinam. Christus ergo vivit in me, id est, regnat in anima mea, et possidet me, facitque me in se vivere. Vivere autem, est actum vitalem habere. Amor vero transponit et mutat amantem in amatum. Dum ergo homo in Christi amore succenditur, crescit et perficitur, moritur in semetipso, quia non agit secundum propriam voluntatem, secundum naturalem inclinationem, secundum privatum amorem, sed secundum divinæ caritatis instinctum, et Christi jussionem atque consilium.
paras.en: [[2:20|And I live, now not I|Vivo autem jam non ego]]: that is, since I have been nailed with Christ to the cross, I live and do not live. For I live not only with the life of nature but of grace; not with a human life but a divine; not with a carnal, worldly and accustomed life, but with a spiritual, heavenly and new one. Therefore he adds: [[2:20|but Christ liveth in me|vivit vero in me Christus]], that is, I do not live or act according to myself, but according to the inspiration, will and teaching of Christ. Christ then lives in me, that is, reigns in my soul, possesses me, and makes me live in him. Now to live is to have vital activity. And love transposes and changes the lover into the beloved. So when a man is kindled, grows and is perfected in the love of Christ, he dies in himself, because he does not act according to his own will, his natural inclination, his private love, but according to the impulse of divine charity and the command and counsel of Christ.

paras.t: Quod autem nunc vivo, id est, bene et meritorie ago, in carne hac fragili, in fide vivo Filii Dei, id est, per virtutem fidei Christi ago, non propria potestate, aut legis subsidio. Justus enim ex fide vivit ; qui vero incredulus est, infideliter agit. Qui dilexit me : sicuti ipse protestatur, Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos ; rursusque per Prophetam, In caritate perpetua dilexi te ; et tradidit semetipsum pro me : prout dicit, Ego sum pastor bonus, et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis. Hinc Propheta : Tradidit, inquit, in mortem animam suam. Ecce quam affectuosissima prorsusque dulcissima verba. Quod enim generaliter pro omnibus factum est, Apostolus propter ardentissimam ad Christum dilectionem, quasi pro se solo, vel singulariter factum æstimat. Nam ut ait Chrysostomus : Hic est affectus servi fidelis, ut quod pro omnibus communiter fecit et pertulit Christus, quasi pro se tantum putet illum fecisse et pertulisse. Et utique merito hoc æstimare debemus, quoniam tanta est Christi misericordia, bonitas, et dilectio ad unumquemque nostrum, ut mallet pro quolibet sigillatim ac singulariter omnia facere et sustinere, quæ pro omnibus simul fecit et passus est, quam aliquem perire, quantum est ex parte ipsius.
paras.en: [[2:20|And that I live now|Quod autem nunc vivo]], that is, act well and meritoriously, [[2:20|in the flesh|in carne]], this frail flesh, [[2:20|I live in the faith of the Son of God|in fide vivo Filii Dei]], that is, I act by the power of faith in Christ, not by my own power or the help of the law. For [[Rom 1:17|the just man liveth by faith|Justus enim ex fide vivit]]; but [[Is 21:2|he that is unfaithful dealeth unfaithfully|qui vero incredulus est, infideliter agit]]. [[2:20|who loved me|Qui dilexit me]]: as he himself declares, [[John 15:9|As the Father hath loved me, I also have loved you|Sicut dilexit me Pater, et ego dilexi vos]]; and again through the Prophet, [[Jer 31:3|I have loved thee with an everlasting love|In caritate perpetua dilexi te]]; [[2:20|and delivered himself for me|et tradidit semetipsum pro me]]: as he says, [[John 10:14|I am the good shepherd|Ego sum pastor bonus]], [[John 10:15|and I lay down my life for my sheep|et animam meam pono pro ovibus meis]]. Hence the Prophet says: [[Is 53:12|he hath delivered his soul unto death|Tradidit, inquit, in mortem animam suam]]. Behold what most affectionate and altogether most sweet words! For what was done for all in general, the Apostle, out of his most ardent love for Christ, regards as done as it were for himself alone, or singly. For as Chrysostom says: This is the affection of a faithful servant, that what Christ did and suffered for all in common, he should think Christ did and suffered as if for him alone. And rightly ought we to think so, since so great is Christ's mercy, goodness and love towards each one of us, that he would rather do and endure for each one singly and individually all that he did and suffered for all together, than that anyone should perish, as far as lies with him.

paras.t: Non abjicio gratiam Dei, id est, caritatem et beneficia divina mihi per Christum collata, non sperno nec desero, legi finaliter inhærendo. Si enim per legem justitia, id est, si virtute et actibus legis homo justificatur, remissionem peccati et gratiæ infusionem adipiscendo, ut Judæi confidunt, ergo Christus gratis, id est sine causa necessaria, et quasi superflue, mortuus est, quum non sit mortuus, secundum Scripturas, nisi propter hominis justificationem, juxta illud propheticum : Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris.
paras.en: [[2:21|I cast not away the grace of God|Non abjicio gratiam Dei]], that is, I do not spurn or forsake the charity and the divine benefits conferred on me through Christ by clinging finally to the law. [[2:21|For if justice be by the law|Si enim per legem justitia]], that is, if man is justified by the power and acts of the law, obtaining remission of sin and infusion of grace, as the Jews trust, [[2:21|then Christ died in vain|ergo gratis Christus mortuus est]], that is, without necessary cause and as it were superfluously; whereas, according to the Scriptures, he died only for man's justification, according to that prophetic word: [[Lam 4:20|The breath of our mouth, Christ the Lord, is taken in our sins|Spiritus oris nostri, Christus Dominus, captus est in peccatis nostris]].

paras.t: Ostensa cessatione legalium ex perfectione evangelicæ legis, nunc idem ostenditur ex imperfectione legis Mosaicæ.
paras.en: Having shown from the perfection of the law of the Gospel that the legal observances [that is, the ceremonial precepts of the Mosaic law] have ceased, he now shows the same from the imperfection of the law of Moses.

paras.t: O insensati, id est stulti insipientesque, Galatæ! Non incurrit Apostolus sententiam Salvatoris, dicentis, Qui dixerit fratri suo, Fatue, reus erit gehennæ ignis: quia non ex contemptu aut malignitate, sed zelo æquitatis et animo corrigendi insensatos eos appellat. Sic enim et Christus dixit discipulis : O stulti et tardi corde ad credendum! Quis vos fascinavit, id est, more magorum ludificavit atque decepit, vel more inficientium oculos falsitatis veneno immutavit et intoxicavit, non obedire veritati, id est veræ prædicationi et justis præceptis evangelicæ disciplinæ, per quam legalia excluduntur? Ante quorum oculos, id est in quorum notitia evidenti, Christus Jesus proscriptus est, id est, ad mortem damnatus, vel aperte descriptus. Hoc enim vobis certissime constat, quod Christus propter nostram salutem adjudicatus est morti, ipseque Christus vobis clare notificatus. Et in vobis est crucifixus, id est, crucifixio ejus cordibus vestris innotuit. Vel, In vobis crucifixus, id est, vestri amore mortem crucis sustinuit. Vel, In vobis crucifixus, id est, vestra infidelitate et culpa rursus quodammodo crucifixus videtur, quia sic peccatis in eum uti qui eum crucifixerunt. Unde et alibi de quibusdam asseritur : Rursus crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei, et ostentui habentes.
paras.en: [[3:1|O senseless|O insensati]], that is, foolish and unwise, [[3:1|Galatians|Galatæ]]! The Apostle does not incur the sentence of the Saviour, who says: Whosoever shall say to his brother, [[Matt 5:22|Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire|Fatue, reus erit gehennæ ignis]] [Denis joins "to his brother" from the clause before]: for it is not out of contempt or malice, but out of zeal for what is right and with the intention of correcting them, that he calls them senseless. For so Christ too said to the disciples: [[Luke 24:25|O foolish and slow of heart to believe|O stulti et tardi corde ad credendum]]! [[3:1|who hath bewitched you|Quis vos fascinavit]], that is, has deluded and deceived you in the manner of magicians, or, in the manner of those who infect the eyes, has altered and poisoned you with the venom of falsehood, [[3:1|that you should not obey the truth|non obedire veritati]], that is, the true preaching and the just precepts of the gospel discipline, by which the legal observances are excluded? [[3:1|before whose eyes|Ante quorum oculos]], that is, in whose clear knowledge, [[3:1|Jesus Christ hath been set forth|Christus Jesus proscriptus est]], that is, condemned to death, or openly portrayed [Denis reads proscriptus, "proscribed", where the Vulgate has præscriptus, "set forth" or "written up"; hence his two senses]. For this is most certainly known to you, that Christ was adjudged to death for our salvation, and that Christ himself was clearly made known to you. And [[3:1|crucified among you|in vobis est crucifixus]], that is, his crucifixion has become known in your hearts. Or, [[3:1|crucified among you|In vobis crucifixus]], that is, for love of you he endured the death of the cross. Or, [[3:1|crucified among you|In vobis crucifixus]], that is, by your unbelief and fault he seems in a manner to be crucified again, because you so sin against him, as did those who crucified him. Hence it is also said elsewhere of certain men: [[Heb 6:6|crucifying again to themselves the Son of God and making him a mockery|Rursus crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium Dei, et ostentui habentes]].

paras.t: Sciendum, quod fascinatio diversis modis accipitur, videlicet, pro magica ludificatione, pro invidia, pro immutatione alterius, quam Avicenna dixit fieri posse sola imaginatione unius in alium : quod Ægidius de Roma in libro contra errores philosophorum, satis redarguit. Fit tamen interdum per quamdam materialem effluxionem humorum nocentium, aerem inficientium : sicut quorumdam urentes infectique oculi teneros lædunt pueros, in tantum ut escam evomant atque fastidiant. Propter quod pueri tales fascinari dicuntur. Pro invidentia quoque sumi videtur, quum in libro Sapientiæ dicitur: Fascinatio malignitatis obscurat bona. Invidus namque non solum sibi ipsi, sed etiam his nocet in quibus aliqua bona esse incipiunt.
paras.en: It should be known that bewitching [Latin fascinatio, the word of the Apostle's "hath bewitched"] is taken in different ways: namely, for magical delusion; for envy; and for an alteration of another, which Avicenna said can be brought about by the imagination of one person alone acting upon another: a view which Giles of Rome sufficiently refutes in his book Against the Errors of the Philosophers. It does, however, sometimes come about through a certain material outflow of harmful humours that infect the air: as the burning and diseased eyes of certain people harm tender children, so much that they vomit their food and loathe it. For this reason such children are said to be bewitched [that is, struck by the evil eye]. It also seems to be taken for envy, when it is said in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 4:12|the bewitching of vanity obscureth good things|Fascinatio malignitatis obscurat bona]] [Denis reads malignitatis, "of malice", where the Vulgate has nugacitatis, "of vanity"]. For the envious man harms not only himself but also those in whom some good things are beginning to be.

paras.t: Hoc solum primo et præcipue volo a vobis discere, id est per modum discentis audire. Loquitur autem Apostolus ironice, et quæritur hoc, non per modum dubitantis, sed admirantis, vel potius ex obliquo apertissimum errorem ostendentis. Ex operibus legis, id est virtute et merito observantiarum legalium, Spiritum Sanctum accepistis in signo visibili (sicut frequenter fiebat in primitiva Ecclesia, quando baptizabantur fideles, et manus Apostolorum eis imponebantur ; vel si Galatæ non receperunt Spiritum Sanctum in signo tali externo, tamen tam copiosam gratiam perceperunt, ut certissime pateret eos recepisse Spiritum Sanctum), an ex auditu fidei, id est ex fide, quæ per auditum acquiritur dispositive, a Deo autem efficienter? Et quoniam certum est quod non receperunt Spiritum ex operibus legis, quia gentiles erant, legem non habentes nec observantes, sed ex fide : nam quum ad Apostoli prædicationem crediderint et baptizati sunt, descendit in eos Spiritus Sanctus, idcirco in observatione legalium non consistit salus ipsorum, aut aliorum gentilium.
paras.en: [[3:2|This only|Hoc solum]], first and foremost, [[3:2|would I learn of you|volo a vobis discere]], that is, hear from you as a learner. Now the Apostle speaks ironically, and asks this not as one in doubt but as one marvelling, or rather as one indirectly pointing out a most obvious error. [[3:2|by the works of the law|Ex operibus legis]], that is, by the power and merit of the legal observances, [[3:2|did you receive the Spirit|Spiritum Sanctum accepistis]] in a visible sign (as often happened in the primitive Church, when the faithful were baptized and the hands of the Apostles were laid upon them[[Acts 8:17||]]; or, if the Galatians did not receive the Holy Ghost in such an outward sign, they nevertheless received so abundant a grace that it was most plainly evident that they had received the Holy Ghost), [[3:2|or by the hearing of faith|an ex auditu fidei]], that is, by faith, which is acquired through hearing[[Rom 10:17||]] dispositively, but from God efficiently [that is, hearing prepares a man for faith, but God is the cause that produces it]? And since it is certain that they did not receive the Spirit from the works of the law, for they were Gentiles, neither having the law nor observing it, but from faith (for when they had believed at the Apostle's preaching and were baptized, the Holy Ghost came down upon them), therefore their salvation, or that of other Gentiles, does not consist in the observance of the legal precepts.

paras.t: Sic stulti estis, id est divinorum cognitione privati, ut quum Spiritu Sancto operante in vobis, cœperitis spiritualiter vivere ; vel, Spiritu, id est a spirituali fervore et interna devotione ; nunc carne consummemini, id est in carnalibus observantiis legis et exterioribus exercitiis perfectionem quæratis, imo carnales et frigidi efficiamini. Hoc modo multi a spiritu ordiuntur, et carnaliter terminant, procedentes ordine retrogrado. Conveniens etenim ordo est, a carnalibus ad spiritualia scandere, non a spiritualibus ad carnalia cadere, sicut iis accidit.
paras.en: [[3:3|Are you so foolish|Sic stulti estis]], that is, deprived of the knowledge of divine things, [[3:3|that, whereas|ut quum]] [[3:3|in the Spirit|Spiritu]], the Holy Ghost working in you, [[3:3|you began|cœperitis]] to live spiritually; or, [[3:3|in the Spirit|Spiritu]], that is, from spiritual fervour and inward devotion; [[3:3|you would now be made perfect by the flesh|nunc carne consummemini]], that is, you seek perfection in the carnal observances of the law and in outward exercises, or rather you become carnal and cold. In this way many begin from the spirit and end carnally, proceeding in a backward order. For the fitting order is to climb from carnal things to spiritual ones, not to fall from spiritual things to carnal ones, as has happened to these.

paras.t: Tanta passi estis, id est, tam vehementer decepti fascinatique estis a falsis, sine causa, id est irrationabiliter ; si tamen sine causa, quia fortassis propter peccata vestra meruistis sic ludificari ; vel Deus propter aliquid melius illud permisit. Vel sic : Tanta passi estis, id est, multa jam adversa passi estis pro Christo, sine causa, id est sine fructu et præmio : nam legalia observando et fallacibus credendo, peccastis mortaliter, et omne meritum perdidistis ; si tamen sine causa : id est, non absolute dico vos illa sine causa perpessos, quoniam pœnitere potestis, sicque reviviscent opera meritoria, quæ ante viva fuerunt.
paras.en: [[3:4|Have you suffered so great things|Tanta passi estis]], that is, have you been so violently deceived and bewitched by false men, [[3:4|in vain|sine causa]], that is, without reason? [[3:4|If it be yet in vain|si tamen sine causa]]: for perhaps you deserved to be so deluded because of your sins; or God permitted it for the sake of some greater good. Or thus: [[3:4|Have you suffered so great things|Tanta passi estis]], that is, have you already suffered many adversities for Christ, [[3:4|in vain|sine causa]], that is, without fruit and reward? For by observing the legal precepts and believing deceivers you have sinned mortally and lost all merit. [[3:4|If it be yet in vain|si tamen sine causa]]: that is, I do not say absolutely that you have suffered those things in vain, since you can do penance, and so the meritorious works which were alive before will live again [that is, the merit of good works, lost by mortal sin, revives with repentance].

paras.t: Qui ergo tribuit vobis Spiritum Sanctum, videlicet Deus Pater, et operatur virtutes, id est opera virtuosa seu signa, in vobis : omnia enim opera nostra operatus est in nobis ; ex operibus legis hoc facit in vobis, an ex auditu fidei? Patet autem quod non ex operibus legis (quæ nunquam perpetrastis) Deus hoc faciat, sed ex auditu fidei, secundum sensum inductum.
paras.en: [[3:5|He therefore who giveth to you the Spirit|Qui ergo tribuit vobis Spiritum Sanctum]], namely God the Father, [[3:5|and worketh miracles|et operatur virtutes]], that is, virtuous works or signs [virtutes means both "virtues" and "mighty works"], [[3:5|among you|in vobis]] (for [[Is 26:12|thou hast wrought all our works for us|omnia enim opera nostra operatus est in nobis]] [Denis puts it in the third person: "he hath wrought"]), [[3:5|doth he do it by the works of the law|ex operibus legis hoc facit]] in you, [[3:5|or by the hearing of the faith|an ex auditu fidei]]? Now it is plain that God does this not from the works of the law (which you never performed), but [[3:5|by the hearing of the faith|ex auditu fidei]], according to the sense implied.

paras.t: Et ad hoc allegat Scripturam et exemplum Abrahæ patriarchæ. Sicut scriptum est : Abraham credidit Deo, sicuti Geneseos testatur historia : credidit enim in spem et contra spem ; et reputatum est ei, secundum divinæ pietatis acceptationem, ad justitiam, id est, actu fidei suæ justificatus est.
paras.en: And for this he brings forward Scripture and the example of the patriarch Abraham. [[3:6|As it is written: Abraham believed God|Sicut scriptum est : Abraham credidit Deo]][[Gen 15:6||]][[Rom 4:3||]], as the history of Genesis testifies: for he [[Rom 4:18|against hope believed in hope|credidit enim in spem et contra spem]]; [[3:6|and it was reputed to him|et reputatum est ei]], by the acceptance of the divine goodness, [[3:6|unto justice|ad justitiam]], that is, he was justified by the act of his faith.

paras.t: Cognoscite ergo, quia qui ex fide sunt, id est, per fidem agunt, et vere fideles consistunt, hi sunt spirituales filii Abrahæ, imitando fidem ac devotionem ipsius. Providens autem, id est prudenter prænuntians, Scriptura, seu Deus in Scripturis, quia ex fide sine cæremonialibus legis justificat gentes conversas, Deus prænuntiavit Abrahæ : Quia benedicentur in te, id est in fidei tuæ imitatione seu Christo ex te nascituro, omnes gentes, id est aliqui de omni genere hominum. Igitur qui ex fide sunt, id est, qui per fidem in Deo esse meritorium habent, benedicentur, id est, divinarum gratiarum collationem recipient, cum fideli Abraham, id est, sicut benedictus est Abraham merito fidei suæ : quamvis et illud meritum fuerit Dei donum, cujus est omne bonum.
paras.en: [[3:7|Know ye, therefore, that they who are of faith|Cognoscite ergo, quia qui ex fide sunt]], that is, who act through faith and stand as true believers, [[3:7|the same are the|hi sunt]] spiritual [[3:7|children of Abraham|filii Abrahæ]], by imitating his faith and devotion. [[3:8|foreseeing|Providens autem]], that is, wisely foretelling, [[3:8|the scripture|Scriptura]], or God in the Scriptures, that [[3:8|by faith|ex fide]], without the ceremonies of the law, [[3:8|God justifieth the Gentiles|justificat gentes]] that are converted, [[3:8|told unto Abraham before|prænuntiavit Abrahæ]]: [[3:8|In thee|Quia benedicentur in te]], that is, in the imitation of thy faith, or in Christ who is to be born of thee, [[3:8|shall all nations be blessed|omnes gentes]][[Gen 22:18||]] [the margin gives Gen. xxii, 18; the words "in thee" are those of Gen 12:3], that is, some of every race of men. [[3:9|Therefore, they that are of faith|Igitur qui ex fide sunt]], that is, who through faith have meritorious being in God, [[3:9|shall be blessed|benedicentur]], that is, shall receive the bestowal of divine graces, [[3:9|with faithful Abraham|cum fideli Abraham]], that is, as Abraham was blessed by the merit of his faith: although that merit too was the gift of God, from whom is every good thing[[Jas 1:17||]].

paras.t: Quod autem ex operibus cæremonialibus legis nemo justificetur, ostenditur. Quicumque enim ex operibus legis sunt, id est, virtute legalium se posse salvari confidunt, sub maledicto sunt, id est, transgressionis periculo subjacent : quam evadere nequeunt, quoniam Christi gratiam non requirunt. Scriptum est enim : Maledictus omnis, vel simpliciter coram Deo, vel reprehensione aliqua dignus est, qui non permanserit per obedientiam in omnibus mandatis quæ scripta sunt in libro legis Moysis, id est in Deuteronomio, ubi resumuntur sub compendio præcepta divina, in aliis Moysis libris præscripta, ut faciat ea, id est, opere impleat, quoad præcepta affirmativa. Hoc autem sine fide et gratia Christi non potuit adimpleri : ideo lex mortem atque damnationem ex occasione operabatur. Jussit enim, et tamen gratiam obediendi non contulit.
paras.en: Next it is shown that no one is justified by the ceremonial works of the law. [[3:10|For as many as are of the works of the law|Quicumque enim ex operibus legis sunt]], that is, who trust that they can be saved by virtue of the legal observances, [[3:10|are under a curse|sub maledicto sunt]], that is, lie under the danger of transgression, which they cannot escape, since they do not seek the grace of Christ. [[3:10|For it is written: Cursed is every one|Scriptum est enim : Maledictus omnis]][[Deut 27:26||]], either simply before God, or as one deserving some reproof, [[3:10|that abideth, not|qui non permanserit]] through obedience [[3:10|in all things|in omnibus mandatis]] commanded [[3:10|which are written in the book of the law|quæ scripta sunt in libro legis]] of Moses, that is, in Deuteronomy, where the divine precepts laid down in the other books of Moses are gathered up again in summary, [[3:10|to do them|ut faciat ea]], that is, to fulfil them in deed, as regards the affirmative precepts [that is, the commandments to do something, as distinct from the prohibitions]. But this could not be fulfilled without faith and the grace of Christ: therefore the law, by occasion, worked death and damnation[[Rom 4:15||]]. For it commanded, and yet did not confer the grace to obey.

paras.t: Quoniam autem in lege scripta, id est virtute et cæremoniis legis, seclusa fide et gratia Christi, videlicet per solam legem et actus ejus exteriores, nemo justificatur apud Deum, qui cordis inspector est infallibilis, manifestum est auctoritate Habacuc prophetæ, qui ait : Quia justus ex fide vivit. Sic enim Scriptura dicit : Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit recta anima ejus in semetipso: justus autem in sua fide vivet. Christus quoque similia his loquitur sæpe, ut est illud: Qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam: et, Fides tua te salvum fecit, etc.
paras.en: [[3:11|But that in the law|Quoniam autem in lege]] written, that is, by the power and ceremonies of the law, faith and the grace of Christ being set aside, namely through the law alone and its outward acts, [[3:11|no man is justified with God|nemo justificatur apud Deum]], who is the unfailing searcher of the heart[[Prov 24:12||]][[Wis 1:6||]], [[3:11|it is manifest|manifestum est]] by the authority of the prophet Habacuc, who says: [[3:11|because the just man liveth by faith|Quia justus ex fide vivit]]. For thus the Scripture says: [[Hab 2:4|Behold, he that is unbelieving, his soul shall not be right in himself: but the just shall live in his faith|Ecce qui incredulus est, non erit recta anima ejus in semetipso: justus autem in sua fide vivet]]. Christ too often says things like these, as in that saying: [[John 6:47|He that believeth in me hath everlasting life|Qui credit in me, habet vitam æternam]]; and: [[Luke 17:19|thy faith hath made thee whole|Fides tua te salvum fecit]], etc.

paras.t: Lex autem, quantum ad cærimonialia, de quibus jam agitur hic, non est ex fide, id est, non principaliter innititur fidei, quum non sit de incomprehensibilibus, quorum est fides : sed qui fecerit ea, id est, cærimonialia jussa impleverit, vivet in illis, id est, corporalis mortis pœnas evadet, sed vitam gratiæ non consequetur, nisi opera illa operata, ex interna caritate et fide ducant originem.
paras.en: [[3:12|But the law|Lex autem]], as regards the ceremonial precepts, which are being dealt with here, [[3:12|is not of faith|non est ex fide]], that is, does not rest chiefly upon faith, since it is not concerned with incomprehensible things, which are the object of faith[[Heb 11:1||]] [the margin gives Hebr. v, 1, which does not fit; faith is defined in Heb 11:1]: [[3:12|but he that doth those things|sed qui fecerit ea]], that is, who has fulfilled the ceremonies commanded, [[3:12|shall live in them|vivet in illis]], that is, shall escape the penalty of bodily death, but shall not obtain the life of grace, unless those works, once done, take their origin from inward charity and faith.

paras.t: Insuper manifestat Apostolus, quod a Christo derivetur ad nos justificatio et benedictio. Christus nos redemit, id est, merito suæ dignissimæ passionis absolvit, de maledicto legis, id est de jugo, damnatione et pœna quam lex transgressoribus infligebat. Absolvit enim nos, id est Judæos, ab obligatione seu debito servandi legem, et per consequens a maledicto sequenti. Factus pro nobis maledictum, id est pro nostra salute maledictionem hominum passus: quia et culpam ei adscripserunt, et pœnam tanquam impio inflixerunt. Quod totum ipse propter nos pati dignatus est, sicut per Psalmistam testatur: Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam; et, Tu scis improperium meum et confusionem meam. Hinc quoque Isaias dixit: Cum sceleratis reputatus est. Quia scriptum est: Maledictus maledictione culpæ, et merito reprobatus, omnis homo qui pendet in ligno pro suis sceleribus. Sed hoc in Christo locum non habet. Quomodo ergo Apostolus applicat auctoritatem istam ad Christum, nisi quantum ad hoc, quod Christus cum ceteris maledictis et impiis crucifixis reputatus est a reprobis, imo et assimilatus per pœnas? Propter quod ait per Prophetam: Æstimatus sum cum descendentibus in lacum; item, Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis.
paras.en: Moreover the Apostle shows that justification and blessing are derived to us from Christ. [[3:13|Christ hath redeemed us|Christus nos redemit]], that is, has set us free by the merit of his most worthy passion, [[3:13|from the curse of the law|de maledicto legis]], that is, from the yoke, condemnation and punishment which the law inflicted on transgressors. For he set us free, that is, the Jews, from the obligation or debt of keeping the law, and consequently from the curse that followed upon it. [[3:13|being made a curse for us|Factus pro nobis maledictum]], that is, suffering the cursing of men for our salvation: for they both ascribed guilt to him and inflicted punishment on him as on a wicked man. All this he deigned to suffer for our sake, as he testifies through the Psalmist: [[Ps 68:5|then did I pay that which I took not away|Quæ non rapui, tunc exsolvebam]]; and: [[Ps 68:20|Thou knowest my reproach, and my confusion|Tu scis improperium meum et confusionem meam]] [the margin gives Ps. xxi, 17; both sayings are from Psalm 68]. Hence Isaias too said that he [[Is 53:12|was reputed with the wicked|Cum sceleratis reputatus est]]. [[3:13|for it is written: Cursed|Quia scriptum est: Maledictus]][[Deut 21:23||]] with the curse of guilt, and deservedly rejected, [[3:13|is every one that hangeth on a tree|omnis homo qui pendet in ligno]] for his own crimes. But this has no place in Christ. How then does the Apostle apply this authority to Christ, except insofar as Christ was reckoned by the reprobate among the other accursed and wicked men who were crucified, and was indeed made like them by his punishments? For this reason he says through the Prophet: [[Ps 87:5|I am counted among them that go down to the pit|Æstimatus sum cum descendentibus in lacum]] [the margin gives Ps. xxxvii; the words are Ps 87:5]; and again: [[Ps 21:7|But I am a worm, and no man: the reproach of men, and the outcast of the people|Ego autem sum vermis et non homo, opprobrium hominum et abjectio plebis]].

paras.t: Itaque Christus nos Judæos redemit de maledicto legis, ut in gentibus, quæ non erant sub legis maledicto, benedictio Abrahæ fieret, id est, gratia Abrahæ promissa diffunderetur, in Christo Jesu, id est virtute et merito Christi, seu per Christum, tanquam per mediatorem ; ut pollicitationem Spiritus, id est æternam felicitatem a Spiritu Sancto (qui nobis datus est in pignus et arrham futuræ beatitudinis) repromissam, accipiamus post præsentis peregrinationis exsilium, per fidem, non per opera legis, quibus lex ab Evangelio distinguitur, puta per cærimonialia seu judicialia : de operibus autem moralibus non est sermo.
paras.en: Therefore [[3:13|Christ hath redeemed us|Christus nos Judæos redemit]] Jews [[3:13|from the curse of the law|de maledicto legis]], that [[3:14|on the Gentiles|ut in gentibus]], who were not under the curse of the law, [[3:14|the blessing of Abraham might come|benedictio Abrahæ fieret]], that is, the grace promised to Abraham might be poured out, [[3:14|through Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, by the power and merit of Christ, or through Christ as through a mediator; that [[3:14|the promise of the Spirit|ut pollicitationem Spiritus]], that is, the eternal happiness promised by the Holy Ghost (who is given to us as a pledge and earnest of the beatitude to come), [[3:14|we may receive|accipiamus]] after the exile of this present pilgrimage, [[3:14|by faith|per fidem]], not by the works of the law by which the law is distinguished from the Gospel, that is, by the ceremonial or judicial precepts: for there is no question here of the moral works.

paras.t: Præterea, probat Apostolus per humanæ consuetudinis observantiam, quod justitia et beatitudo et Spiritus Sanctus debetur per fidem, non per opera legis. Fratres (secundum hominem dico, id est, per humanam consuetudinem probo quod dixi), tamen hominis testamentum confirmatum nemo spernit : id est, quamvis in rebus humanis sit magna instabilitas, tamen hominis cujuscumque testamentum, id est ordinationem de successione hereditatis, confirmatum testibus, signis, seu morte testatoris (testamentum enim in mortuis confirmatum, imo et immobilitatum est), nemo spernit tanquam invalidum ; aut superordinat, id est, aliquid ei adjungit, aut de rebus alio modo disponit, si tamen sit homo rationabiliter agens, fueritque testamentum rite peractum. Multo igitur fortius divinæ dispositiones seu promissiones firmæ erunt et invariabiles. De quibus subjungitur :
paras.en: Further, the Apostle proves from the observance of human custom that justice and beatitude and the Holy Ghost are due through faith, not through the works of the law. [[3:15|Brethren|Fratres]] ([[3:15|I speak after the manner of man|secundum hominem dico]], that is, I prove what I have said from human custom), [[3:15|yet a man's testament, if it be confirmed, no man despiseth|tamen hominis testamentum confirmatum nemo spernit]]: that is, although there is great instability in human affairs, yet the testament of any man whatever, that is, his disposition for the succession to his inheritance, once confirmed by witnesses, seals, or the death of the testator (for [[Heb 9:17|a testament is of force after men are dead|testamentum enim in mortuis confirmatum]], and indeed made unchangeable), no man despises as invalid; [[3:15|nor addeth to it|aut superordinat]] [superordinat, literally "ordains over it"], that is, adds something to it, or disposes of the goods in another way, provided he be a man acting reasonably and the testament has been duly made. Much more, then, will the divine dispositions or promises be firm and unchangeable. Of these it is added:

paras.t: Abrahæ dicta, id est divinitus factæ, sunt promissiones diversæ, vel una frequenter, ut patet in diversis capitulis libri Geneseos. Facta est enim ei promissio de possessione Terræ sanctæ, per quam mystice designatur possessio terræ viventium seu patriæ Beatorum ; de innumerabili quoque multiplicatione seminis sui, præsertim spiritualis, id est fidelium qui per fidem ejus filii sunt ; et quod in semine suo benedicerentur omnes gentes. Et semini ejus, id est Christo filio Abrahæ secundum naturam assumptam, factæ sunt promissiones : non quod ad eum fiebant, sed quoniam pertinebant ad eum, tanquam implendæ per ipsum. Per Christum namque data est benedictio omnibus gentibus, quæ erat principalis promissio Abrahæ facta. Ideo subditur : Non dicit Scriptura Geneseos, In seminibus, quasi in multis, id est, promissionem factam semini Abrahæ Scriptura non exprimit pluraliter, dicendo ad Abraham, In seminibus tuis benedicentur omnes gentes : quod faceret, si de pluribus loqueretur ; sed quasi in uno, id est, singulariter nominat semen istud, dicendo : Et semini tuo, qui est Christus, id est, in Christo ex te nato benedicentur omnes gentes. Sic enim ad Abraham dictum est : In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes.
paras.en: [[3:16|To Abraham were|Abrahæ dicta]] spoken, that is, made by God, [[3:16|the promises|sunt promissiones]]: several of them, or one made often, as appears in various chapters of the book of Genesis. For there was made to him the promise of the possession of the Holy Land[[Gen 15:7||]][[Gen 17:8||]], by which is mystically signified the possession of the land of the living, that is, of the homeland of the Blessed; and also of the countless multiplication of his seed[[Gen 22:17||]], especially of his spiritual seed, that is, of the faithful, who through faith are his children; and that in his seed all nations should be blessed[[Gen 12:3||]][[Gen 18:18||]][[Gen 22:18||]]. [[3:16|and to his seed|Et semini ejus]], that is, to Christ, the son of Abraham according to the nature he assumed, were the promises made: not that they were made to him, but because they concerned him, as to be fulfilled through him. For through Christ the blessing was given to all nations, which was the chief promise made to Abraham. Therefore it is added: [[3:16|He saith not|Non dicit]] (that is, the Scripture of Genesis) [[3:16|And to his seeds as of many|In seminibus, quasi in multis]], that is, the Scripture does not express in the plural the promise made to the seed of Abraham, by saying to Abraham, In thy seeds shall all nations be blessed, as it would if it were speaking of many; [[3:16|But as of one|sed quasi in uno]], that is, it names this seed in the singular, saying: [[3:16|And to thy seed, which is Christ|Et semini tuo, qui est Christus]], that is, in Christ born of thee shall all nations be blessed. For so it was said to Abraham: [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes]].

paras.t: Hoc autem dico quod subditur, scilicet : Testamentum confirmatum a Deo, id est promissionem ad Abraham factam, per Christum implendam, videlicet de omnium gentium benedictione in Christo, quæ post quadringentos et triginta annos facta est lex, id est lex scripta quæ facta est, id est Moysi data in monte Sinai, post quadringentos et triginta annos a tempore promissionis quæ primo facta est Abrahæ venienti de terra Chaldæorum, non irritum facit, id est, promissionem prædictam divino juramento firmatam non falsificat, ad evacuandam promissionem hanc suo effectu, videlicet impediendo impletionem ipsius : quod tamen faceret, si per legem daretur benedictio illa, quæ est hereditas sempiterna. Hæc enim promissio Abrahæ facta, et per semen ejus (id est Christum) implenda, diu præcessit legislationem. Si ergo bonum per eam promissum, puta benedictio hæc, daretur per legem, primo sequeretur quod non esset ex promissione ; secundo, quod frustra fieret mentio de semine Abrahæ, qui est Christus ; tertio, quod Abraham, Isaac, Jacob et cæteri Sancti qui ante legem fuerunt, divina benedictione caruissent, neque æternam hereditatem essent adepti. Unde certissime liquet quod a principio mundi, per fidem Christi futuri dabatur hominibus benedictio gratiæ et salutis.
paras.en: [[3:17|Now this I say|Hoc autem dico]], namely what follows: [[3:17|that the testament which was confirmed by God|Testamentum confirmatum a Deo]], that is, the promise made to Abraham, to be fulfilled through Christ, namely of the blessing of all nations in Christ, [[3:17|the law which was made after four hundred and thirty years|quæ post quadringentos et triginta annos facta est lex]], that is, the written law, which was made, that is, given to Moses on Mount Sinai, four hundred and thirty years after the time of the promise first made to Abraham as he came out of the land of the Chaldeans, [[3:17|doth not disannul|non irritum facit]], that is, does not make false the aforesaid promise, confirmed by a divine oath, [[3:17|to make the promise of no effect|ad evacuandam promissionem]], that is, to empty this promise of its effect, namely by hindering its fulfilment: which it would do, however, if that blessing, which is the everlasting inheritance, were given through the law. For this promise, made to Abraham and to be fulfilled through his seed (that is, Christ), long preceded the giving of the law. If then the good promised through it, that is, this blessing, were given through the law, it would follow, first, that it was not from the promise; secondly, that mention of the seed of Abraham, who is Christ, was made in vain; thirdly, that Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the other saints who lived before the law had lacked the divine blessing and had not obtained the eternal inheritance. Hence it is most certainly clear that from the beginning of the world the blessing of grace and salvation was given to men through faith in the Christ who was to come.

paras.t: Sed quæri potest, quomodo ei quod nunc dicit Apostolus, legem datam post annos quadringentos et triginta a promissione Abrahæ facta, concordet quod idem dicit Apostolus in Actibus : Sorte distribuit eis terram eorum, quasi post quadringentos et quinquaginta annos. Lex enim data est primo anno egressionis ab Ægypto ; distributio vero terræ facta est post quadraginta annos ab egressione prædicta : et ita secundum ratiocinationem hic habitam, distributio terræ facta esset post annos quadringentos et septuaginta, vel circiter. Quæritur etiam, quomodo iis concordet quod legitur in Exodo : Habitatio autem filiorum Israel qua manserunt in Ægypto, fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum, quibus expletis, eodem die egressi sunt. Si enim tamdiu in Ægypto manserunt, non poterunt anni de quibus jam tractat Apostolus, computari a promissione Abrahæ facta, sed ab ingressu Jacob in Ægyptum. — Et respondendum, quod anni de quibus Moyses in Exodo loquitur, secundum doctores, computantur a promissione primo facta Abrahæ usque ad legislationem. Porro ab exitu Abrahæ de Chaldæis, quum primo facta est ei divina promissio, usque ad descensum Jacob in terram Ægypti, fluxerunt anni ducenti et quindecim ; deinde usque ad mortem Joseph anni septuaginta unus ; inde usque ad egressum de Ægypto, centum quadraginta quatuor : qui simul juncti, prædictum numerum constituunt. Anni vero de quibus in Actibus legitur, computantur ab alio exordio, scilicet a nativitate Isaac, secundum Bedam, quando et dictum est Abrahæ quod semen suum accola esset in terra aliena annis quadringentis. Hæc secundum alios dicta sunt. Non enim apposui cor meum hac vice ad considerandum tempora ista attentius.
paras.en: But it may be asked how what the Apostle now says, that the law was given four hundred and thirty years after the promise made to Abraham, agrees with what the same Apostle says in the Acts: he [[Acts 13:19|divided their land among them by lot|Sorte distribuit eis terram eorum]], [[Acts 13:20|As it were, after four hundred and fifty years|quasi post quadringentos et quinquaginta annos]]. For the law was given in the first year of the going out from Egypt, while the distribution of the land was made forty years after that going out: and so, by the reckoning held here, the distribution of the land would have been made after four hundred and seventy years, or thereabouts. It is also asked how these things agree with what is read in Exodus: [[Ex 12:40|And the abode of the children of Israel that they made in Egypt, was four hundred and thirty years|Habitatio autem filiorum Israel qua manserunt in Ægypto, fuit quadringentorum triginta annorum]], [[Ex 12:41|Which being expired, the same day|quibus expletis, eodem die]] they went forth. For if they stayed so long in Egypt, the years of which the Apostle is now treating cannot be reckoned from the promise made to Abraham, but from Jacob's entry into Egypt. — And the answer is that the years of which Moses speaks in Exodus are reckoned, according to the doctors, from the promise first made to Abraham up to the giving of the law. For from Abraham's going out from the Chaldeans, when the divine promise was first made to him, to Jacob's descent into the land of Egypt, two hundred and fifteen years passed; then to the death of Joseph, seventy-one years; thence to the going out from Egypt, one hundred and forty-four: which together make up the number stated. But the years read of in the Acts are reckoned from another starting point, namely from the birth of Isaac, according to Bede, when it was also said to Abraham that his seed would be a sojourner in a strange land for four hundred years[[Gen 15:13||]]. These things have been said following others. For on this occasion I have not set my heart to consider these times more attentively.

paras.t: Quod autem promissio evacuaretur, si ex lege esset benedictio, pandit Apostolus. Nam si ex lege daretur hereditas, id est benedictio gratiæ, seu vita felicitasque æterna, jam non ex promissione daretur, sed ex alia causa, videlicet lege, et ita Abraham esset frustratus spe sua : quod dici non potest, sicut subjungitur. Abrahæ autem per repromissionem de Christo ei sæpius factam, seu per fidem Christi promissi, donavit Deus hereditariam benedictionem cœlestem : de qua ad eum dicebat, Ego protector tuus sum, et merces tua magna nimis.
paras.en: That the promise would be made void if the blessing were from the law, the Apostle makes plain. [[3:18|For if the inheritance be of the law|Nam si ex lege daretur hereditas]], that is, the blessing of grace, or eternal life and happiness, [[3:18|it is no more of promise|jam non ex promissione]] that it would be given, but from another cause, namely the law; and so Abraham would have been cheated of his hope: which cannot be said, as is added. But [[3:18|to Abraham by promise|Abrahæ autem per repromissionem]] made to him often concerning Christ, or through faith in the promised Christ, [[3:18|God gave|donavit Deus]] the heavenly blessing of the inheritance, of which he said to him: [[Gen 15:1|I am thy protector, and thy reward exceeding great|Ego protector tuus sum, et merces tua magna nimis]].

paras.t: Sed quia ex dictis sequi videtur quod lex omnino erat inutilis, quærit Apostolus, ut nostræ dubitationi respondeat : Quid igitur lex? id est, cur data est, et quæ ejus utilitas? Et respondet : Propter transgressiones, id est peccata hominum reprimenda ac punienda, posita est, quatenus homines saltem timore pœnarum quæ determinantur in lege, retraherentur a vitiis, donec veniret semen, id est, Christus per incarnationem mundum intraret, cui repromiserat, id est, de quo Deus promisit quod per ipsum implerentur promissiones divinæ, sicut ad Abraham dixit : In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes. Lex, inquam, ordinata, id est ordinate collata a Deo, per angelos Moysi. Unde Stephanus dicebat Judæis : Accepistis legem in dispositione angelorum. In manu mediatoris, id est, lex ista posita est in potestate Christi, ita ut ipse eam posset mutare, et ei finem imponere, nec esset necessario ei subjectus. Propter quod aiebat : Dominus est Filius hominis, etiam sabbati. Sic communiter exponitur. Sed videtur hoc loco per mediatorem, Moyses posse intelligi, per cujus manum, id est ministerium, data est lex. Moyses enim inter Deum et populum Israel fuerat mediator, sicut et ipse interdum testatur. Constat ergo quod lex data sit Moysi, non solum unius ministerio angeli, sed multorum, quamvis communiter non fiat mentio in libris Moysis nisi de angelo singulariter, qui etiam frequenter Dominus nominatur, cujus persona apparuit ac loquebatur.
paras.en: But since it seems to follow from what has been said that the law was altogether useless, the Apostle asks, so as to answer our doubt: [[3:19|Why then was the law?|Quid igitur lex?]] that is, why was it given, and what is its use? And he answers: [[3:19|because of transgressions|Propter transgressiones]], that is, to restrain and punish the sins of men, [[3:19|It was set|posita est]], so that men, at least through fear of the punishments laid down in the law, might be held back from vices, [[3:19|until the seed should come|donec veniret semen]], that is, until Christ should enter the world by the incarnation, [[3:19|to whom he made the promise|cui repromiserat]], that is, concerning whom God promised that through him the divine promises would be fulfilled, as he said to Abraham: [[Gen 22:18|in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|In semine tuo benedicentur omnes gentes]]. The law, I say, [[3:19|being ordained|ordinata]], that is, bestowed in due order by God, [[3:19|by angels|per angelos]] upon Moses. Hence Stephen said to the Jews: You [[Acts 7:53|have received the law by the disposition of angels|Accepistis legem in dispositione angelorum]]. [[3:19|in the hand of a mediator|In manu mediatoris]], that is, this law was placed in the power of Christ, so that he could change it and put an end to it, and was not of necessity subject to it. For this reason he said: [[Mark 2:28|the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath also|Dominus est Filius hominis, etiam sabbati]]. So it is commonly explained. But in this place Moses seems able to be understood by the mediator, by whose hand, that is, ministry, the law was given. For Moses had been mediator between God and the people of Israel, as he himself sometimes testifies. It is clear, then, that the law was given to Moses by the ministry not of one angel only, but of many, although in the books of Moses mention is commonly made only of an angel in the singular, who is also often called Lord, since it was the Lord's person that appeared and spoke [that is, the angel appeared and spoke in the person of the Lord].

paras.t: Mediator autem unius non est dumtaxat, sed duorum extremorum, inter quæ mediat, et ea connectit ; Deus autem unus est in essentia. Tanquam dicat : Licet Christus sit mediator Dei et hominum, est tamen idem Deus cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto.
paras.en: [[3:20|Now a mediator is not of one|Mediator autem unius non est]] only, but of two extremes, between which he mediates and which he joins together; [[3:20|but God is one|Deus autem unus est]] in essence. As if he said: Although Christ is [[1 Tim 2:5|mediator of God and men|mediator Dei et hominum]], yet he is the same God with the Father and the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Lex ergo adversus promissa Dei? id est, quum lex propter transgressiones posita sit, numquid ex hoc sequitur legem esse contrariam promissioni divinæ, ita ut irritam faciat eam, eo quod ex ipsa lege detur hereditas sempiterna, et non potius ex promissione divina, sicut promissionis forma continuit? Absit. Quod si ita esset, lex promissionem excluderet ; sed quod non sit ita, subjungitur : Si enim data esset per Moysen lex quæ posset vivificare, vitam gratiæ conferendo ; vere ex lege, id est observantia legis, esset justitia infusa et meritoria, quæ efficit dignum vita æterna, et non ex promissione.
paras.en: [[3:21|Was the law then against the promises of God|Lex ergo adversus promissa Dei]]? that is, since the law was [[3:19|set because of transgressions|propter transgressiones posita]], does it follow from this that the law is contrary to the divine promise, so as to make it void, in that the everlasting inheritance would be given from the law itself, and not rather from the divine promise, as the form of the promise contained? [[3:21|God forbid!|Absit.]] If it were so, the law would exclude the promise; but that it is not so is added: [[3:21|For if there had been a law given|Si enim data esset]] through Moses [[3:21|which could give life|lex quæ posset vivificare]], by conferring the life of grace, [[3:21|verily|vere]] [[3:21|by the law|ex lege]], that is, by the observance of the law, [[3:21|justice should have been|esset justitia]], justice infused and meritorious, which makes a man worthy of eternal life, and not by the promise.

paras.t: Sed conclusit, id est, esse ostendit, convicit, et accidenter fecit, Scriptura, id est lex scripta, omnia genera hominum, seu omnes Judæos, sub peccato, non solum originali, sed etiam actuali. Per legem enim erat peccati cognitio directe, et item peccati augmentatio indirecte : primo, quia in vetitum nituntur ; secundo, quia post prohibitionem peccare, gravius est quam ante. Ut promissio, id est promissa beatitudo et gratia, ex fide Jesu Christi daretur credentibus. Per fidem enim Christi salutem consequimur.
paras.en: But [[3:22|the scripture|Scriptura]], that is, the written law, [[3:22|hath concluded|conclusit]] (that is, has shown to be, has convicted, and has incidentally made to be [that is, not by its purpose but by occasion]) [[3:22|all|omnia]] kinds of men, or all the Jews, [[3:22|under sin|sub peccato]][[Rom 3:9||]][[Rom 11:32||]], not only original but also actual. For through the law there was knowledge of sin directly, and likewise an increase of sin indirectly: first, because men strive toward what is forbidden; secondly, because to sin after a prohibition is graver than before. [[3:22|that the promise|Ut promissio]], that is, the promised beatitude and grace, [[3:22|by the faith of Jesus Christ, might be given to them that believe|ex fide Jesu Christi daretur credentibus]]. For it is through faith in Christ that we attain salvation.

paras.t: Ostenso quod lex retraxit a malo, jam declarat quod disponebat ad bonum. Prius autem quam veniret fides christiana, id est, antequam catholica fides publicata fuisset, sub lege custodiebamur, id est, per legis observationem ab adversariis nostræ salutis protegebamur, conclusi, id est de necessitate inducti, nos Judæi de quibus ista dicuntur, […] revelanda erat, id est in fidem catholicam, in qua publice credenda proponuntur quæ in veteri Testamento occultabantur. Non enim potuerunt Judæi per legem salvari, nisi habendo fidem de Christi adventu : ita ut ad fidem confugere cogerentur.
paras.en: Having shown that the law held men back from evil, he now declares that it disposed them to good. [[3:23|But before the faith came|Prius autem quam veniret fides]], the Christian faith, that is, before the catholic faith had been made public, [[3:23|we were kept under the law|sub lege custodiebamur]], that is, we were protected through the observance of the law from the enemies of our salvation, [[3:23|shut up|conclusi]], that is, led on by necessity, we Jews of whom these things are said, […] [some words are lost here, probably the words of the Apostle "unto that faith which"] [[3:23|was to be revealed|revelanda erat]], that is, into the catholic faith, in which the things that were hidden in the Old Testament are publicly set forth to be believed. For the Jews could not be saved through the law except by having faith in the coming of Christ: so that they were compelled to take refuge in faith.

paras.t: Itaque lex pædagogus, id est manuductor, noster, scilicet Judæorum, fuit in Christo Jesu, id est secundum Christi voluntatem ac dispositionem, qui ita instituit, ut Judæi per legem quasi manuducerentur ac dirigerentur ad Salvatorem et fidem explicitam ; vel, In Christo Jesu, id est in observationibus mandatorum a Christo datorum, sine quibus lex nullum ad vitam perduxit ; ut ex fide justificemur, credendo in Christum. Dicitur autem pædagogus proprie ductor puerorum seu pueri, a παιδὸς, quod est puer, et ἀγωγή, ductio. Quemadmodum ergo pædagogus puerum insolentem et imperfectum ad perfectionem perducit, vitia ejus per pœnas et minas comprimendo, sic lex populum Israel carnalem ac rudem præparavit ad Christum.
paras.en: [[3:24|Wherefore the law was our pedagogue|Itaque lex pædagogus]] (that is, our guide leading us by the hand: ours, namely of the Jews) [[3:24|in Christ|fuit in Christo Jesu]], that is, according to the will and disposition of Christ, who so ordained it that the Jews should be led as it were by the hand through the law and directed to the Saviour and to explicit faith; or, [[3:24|in Christ|In Christo Jesu]], that is, in the observance of the commandments given by Christ, without which the law brought no one to life[[Rom 10:4||]]; [[3:24|that we might be justified by faith|ut ex fide justificemur]], by believing in Christ. Now a pedagogue properly means one who leads boys, or a boy, from παιδὸς, which means "boy", and ἀγωγή, "leading". As therefore a pedagogue brings an unruly and imperfect boy to perfection by curbing his faults with punishments and threats, so the law prepared the carnal and untaught people of Israel for Christ.

paras.t: Consequenter tangitur legis cessatio. At ubi, id est quando seu postquam, venit fides catholica, id est, quum promulgata est fides evangelica, jam non sumus sub pædagogo, id est, ad legis custodiam non tenemur.
paras.en: Next the cessation of the law is touched upon. [[3:25|But after|At ubi]], that is, when or after, [[3:25|the faith is come|venit fides]], the catholic faith, that is, when the gospel faith was promulgated, [[3:25|we are no longer under a pedagogue|jam non sumus sub pædagogo]], that is, we are not bound to keep the law.

paras.t: Omnes enim filii Dei estis adoptivi per fidem formatam, in Christo Jesu, id est per fidem Christi, seu existentem in Christo sicut in objecto. Unde Joannes evangelista testatur : Quotquot receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri.
paras.en: [[3:26|For you are all the children of God|Omnes enim filii Dei estis]], adopted children, [[3:26|by faith|per fidem]], formed faith [that is, faith given its form, or life, by charity], [[3:26|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]], that is, by faith in Christ, or faith resting in Christ as in its object. Hence John the Evangelist testifies: [[John 1:12|as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God|Quotquot receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri]].

paras.t: Quicumque enim in Christo, id est in nomine Christi, vel in forma a Christo præscripta, videlicet, in nomine Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti, baptizati estis, Christum spiritualiter induistis, id est, gratia ejus ornati, ejusque passioni ac morti conformati estis, habentes Christum in cordibus vestris morantem. De hac materia plenius dictum est supra ad Romanos.
paras.en: [[3:27|For as many of you as|Quicumque enim]] [[3:27|in Christ|in Christo]], that is, in the name of Christ, or in the form prescribed by Christ, namely, [[Matt 28:19|in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Ghost|in nomine Patris et Filii et Spiritus Sancti]], [[3:27|have been baptized|baptizati estis]], [[3:27|have put on Christ|Christum spiritualiter induistis]] spiritually, that is, you have been adorned with his grace and conformed to his passion and death, having Christ dwelling in your hearts. Of this matter more has been said above, on Romans[[Rom 6:3||]].

paras.t: Non est Judæus neque Græcus, non est servus neque liber, non est masculus neque femina, id est, diversitas generis, conditionis et sexus, nil facit quantum ad fidei statum et dignitatem. Non enim propter ista est alius melior alio, sed propter dona infusa et supernaturalia. Omnes enim vos baptizati, cujuscumque sitis generis, conditionis aut sexus, unum estis per fidem et caritatem, et unum mysticum corpus, in Christo Jesu : secundum quod ipse orabat : Pater, rogo ut omnes sint unum, sicut tu, Pater, in me, et ego in te, ut sint consummati in unum.
paras.en: [[3:28|There is neither Jew nor Greek: there is neither bond nor free: there is neither male nor female|Non est Judæus neque Græcus, non est servus neque liber, non est masculus neque femina]], that is, difference of race, condition and sex counts for nothing as regards the state and dignity of faith[[Acts 10:34||]][[Acts 10:35||]]. For no one is better than another on account of these things, but on account of infused and supernatural gifts. [[3:28|For you are all|Omnes enim vos]] who are baptized, of whatever race, condition or sex you may be, [[3:28|one|unum estis]] through faith and charity, and one mystical body, [[3:28|in Christ Jesus|in Christo Jesu]]: according to what he himself prayed: Father, I pray [[John 17:21|That they all may be one, as thou, Father, in me, and I in thee|ut omnes sint unum, sicut tu, Pater, in me, et ego in te]], [[John 17:23|that they may be made perfect in one|ut sint consummati in unum]].

paras.t: Si autem vos Christi estis, id est, per fidem et gratiam ad Christum pertinetis, ergo semen Abrahæ estis, id est spirituales filii ejus, sectando ipsius vestigia ; secundum promissionem Abrahæ factam, heredes vitæ æternæ, id est, futuræ beatitudinis possessores eritis, sicut promissum est Abrahæ. Si enim filii, et heredes. Eadem quoque ratione fideles vocari possunt filii Jacob, Isaac, atque similium Prophetarum et Patriarcharum. De cessatione autem legis præfata dicit Salvator : Lex et Prophetæ usque ad Joannem Baptistam.
paras.en: [[3:29|And if you be Christ's|Si autem vos Christi estis]], that is, belong to Christ through faith and grace, [[3:29|then are you the seed of Abraham|ergo semen Abrahæ estis]], that is, his spiritual children, by following in his footsteps; [[3:29|according to the promise|secundum promissionem]] made to Abraham, [[3:29|heirs|heredes]] of eternal life, that is, you will be possessors of the beatitude to come, as was promised to Abraham. For [[Rom 8:17|if sons, heirs also|Si enim filii, et heredes]]. By the same reasoning the faithful can also be called children of Jacob, of Isaac, and of the like Prophets and Patriarchs. And of the aforesaid cessation of the law the Saviour says: [[Luke 16:16|The law and the prophets were until John|Lex et Prophetæ usque ad Joannem]] the Baptist.

4.title: Elucidatio capituli quarti: Dico autem quanto tempore heres parvulus est
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: Now I say: as long as the heir is a child
4.note: Much text is lost in the transcription at vv. 22–25, 29 and 30. Please check against the scan.

paras.t: Probata legis cessatione per exempla et rationes, nunc idem ostenditur per humanæ consuetudinis similitudinem. Dico autem quod subditur, scilicet: Quanto tempore, id est quamdiu, heres parvulus est, id est infra annos discretionis, nihil differt a servo, quantum ad liberum usum hereditatis sibi relictæ, sed cogitur disciplinari rigore, nec aliquid facere aut propria dispensare permittitur, nisi juxta voluntatem eorum quibus a parentibus est commissus, quum sit dominus omnium, id est, quamvis tota hereditas ad eum pertineat; sed sub tutoribus, id est defensoribus, qui eum ab adversariis protegant, et actoribus, id est causatoribus seu curatoribus, qui causas ejus expediant eumque in moribus instruant, et usque ad præfinitum, id est determinatum, tempus a patre ejus, videlicet usque ad annos discretionis, vel amplius, prout patri placuerit. Solebant enim antiquitus patres morituri determinare, ut usque ad illud vel illud tempus, filii sub tutorum et actorum dominio essent.
paras.en: Having proved the cessation of the law by examples and reasons, he now shows the same by a likeness drawn from human custom. *Now I say* [Latin *Dico autem*, words of the Vulgate not rendered in the Douay-Rheims] what follows, namely: [[4:1|As long as|Quanto tempore]], that is, for so long as, [[4:1|the heir is a child|heres parvulus est]], that is, under the years of discretion, [[4:1|he differeth nothing from a servant|nihil differt a servo]] as to the free use of the inheritance left to him; but he is held under strict discipline, and is not allowed to do anything or to dispose of his own goods except according to the will of those to whom his parents have entrusted him, [[4:1|though he be lord of all|quum sit dominus omnium]], that is, although the whole inheritance belongs to him; [[4:2|But is under tutors|sed sub tutoribus]], that is, defenders, to protect him from adversaries, [[4:2|and governors|et actoribus]] [Latin *actores*, those who conduct another's affairs or lawsuits], that is, advocates or curators, to dispatch his affairs and instruct him in good conduct, [[4:2|until the time appointed|et usque ad præfinitum]], that is, determined, [[4:2|by the father|tempus a patre]] his father, namely until the years of discretion, or longer, as it pleased the father. For in ancient times fathers about to die used to determine that their sons should be under the authority of tutors and governors until this or that time.

paras.t: Ita et nos Judæi, quum essemus parvuli, id est virtutibus imperfecti, et in divinorum notitia modici, sub elementis mundi hujus, id est sub cærimonialibus legis præceptis, eramus servientes Domino Deo, servitute incompleta et superficiali. Dicuntur autem præcepta cærimonialia, elementa, quoniam erant quædam primordiales institutiones ad fidem atque justitiam. Appellantur quoque elementa mundi, quia terrena bona habebant in præmium, secundum legis promissa. Hæc autem legalia, sub quibus Domino ministrabant Judæi, eis erant tutores, id est contra dæmonum insidias defensores; et actores, quoniam causam eorum coram Deo agebant, qui per sacrificia placabatur.
paras.en: [[4:3|So we also|Ita et nos]] Jews, [[4:3|when we were children|quum essemus parvuli]], that is, imperfect in virtues and slight in the knowledge of divine things, [[4:3|under the elements of the world|sub elementis mundi hujus]] [Denis reads "of this world"], that is, under the ceremonial precepts of the law, [[4:3|were serving|eramus servientes]] the Lord God, with an incomplete and superficial service. Now the ceremonial precepts are called elements because they were certain first rudiments leading to faith and justice. They are also called elements of the world because they had earthly goods for their reward, according to the promises of the law. And these legal ordinances, under which the Jews ministered to the Lord, were their tutors, that is, defenders against the snares of the demons; and their governors, since they pleaded their cause before God, who was appeased by sacrifices.

paras.t: At ubi venit plenitudo temporis, id est, statim quum adimpletum est tempus divinitus præordinatum ut in eo Filius Dei fieret homo, misit Deus Pater paterna auctoritate, id est, in mundo visibiliter apparere conversarique voluit, Filium suum unigenitum, sibi consubstantialem, coæternum et coæqualem. Non itaque misit Pater Filium suum, quasi Filius in sui missione locum mutaverit, quum sit immensus et omnia implens, sicut et Pater; sed idcirco missus dicitur, quoniam Patre volente et operante, carnem assumpsit, atque in mundo novo modo apparuit. Factum, id est genitum, secundum assumptam naturam, ex muliere, inviolata Virgine benedicta, de qua Jeremias vaticinabatur: Novum creavit Dominus super terram: Mulier circumdabit virum. Est autem Hebræi idiomatis consuetudo, ut quæcumque feminei sexus persona, mulier nuncupetur. Factum sub lege, id est legis præceptis sponte subjectum, in circumcisione, oblatione, et aliis multis. Ut eos qui sub lege erant, id est Judæos legalibus mandatis adstrictos, redimeret merito suæ humilitatis ac passionis, non solum a morte peccati et gehennæ, sed etiam a legalium observatione, ut adoptionem filiorum, id est effectum adoptionis divinæ qua adoptantur homines a Deo, videlicet gratiam gratificantem in præsenti, et gloriam consummantem in cœlo, reciperemus. Christi enim descensio, nostri est sublimatio: et ejus incarnatio, nostri utique deificatio creditur. Hæc de visibili missione Filii Dei inducta sunt. Est autem et alia, videlicet invisibilis missio Filii Dei, qua ad animas sanctas atque fideles increata Dei Sapientia mittitur, juxta illud Sapientiæ: Mitte illam de cœlis sanctis tuis, ut mecum sit, et mecum laboret.
paras.en: [[4:4|But when the fulness of the time was come|At ubi venit plenitudo temporis]], that is, as soon as the time divinely foreordained for the Son of God to become man in it had been fulfilled, [[4:4|God sent|misit Deus]] the Father, by His fatherly authority (that is, He willed Him to appear and to dwell visibly in the world), [[4:4|his Son|Filium suum]], the only-begotten, consubstantial with Himself, co-eternal and co-equal. So the Father did not send His Son as though the Son changed place in being sent, since He is immeasurable and fills all things, as the Father does; but He is said to be sent because, by the Father's will and working, He took flesh and appeared in the world in a new way. [[4:4|made|Factum]], that is, begotten according to the nature He assumed, [[4:4|of a woman|ex muliere]], the inviolate and blessed Virgin, of whom Jeremias prophesied: [[Jer 31:22|the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth|Novum creavit Dominus super terram]]: [[Jer 31:22|A WOMAN SHALL COMPASS A MAN|Mulier circumdabit virum]]. Now it is a custom of the Hebrew idiom that any person of the female sex is called a woman. [[4:4|made under the law|Factum sub lege]], that is, of His own will subject to the precepts of the law, in circumcision, in the offering [in the temple], and in many other things. [[4:5|That he might redeem|redimeret]] [[4:5|them who were under the law|Ut eos qui sub lege erant]], that is, the Jews bound by the commandments of the law, by the merit of His humility and passion, not only from the death of sin and of hell, but also from the observance of the legal ordinances: [[4:5|that we might receive|reciperemus]] [[4:5|the adoption of sons|ut adoptionem filiorum]], that is, the effect of the divine adoption by which men are adopted by God, namely sanctifying grace [*gratia gratificans*, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God] in the present, and consummating glory in heaven. For Christ's descent is our exaltation, and His incarnation is believed to be indeed our deification. These things have been brought forward concerning the visible mission of the Son of God. But there is also another, namely the invisible mission of the Son of God, by which the uncreated Wisdom of God is sent to holy and faithful souls, according to that of Wisdom: [[Wis 9:10|Send her out of thy holy heaven|Mitte illam de cœlis sanctis tuis]], [[Wis 9:10|that she may be with me, and may labour with me|ut mecum sit, et mecum laboret]].

paras.t: Porro quid ex divina adoptione sequatur in nobis, pandit Apostolus. Quoniam autem estis, o Galatæ ceterique fideles, filii Dei adoptivi ab æterno electi, idcirco in signum filiationis istius, misit Deus Pater Spiritum Filii sui, id est Spiritum Sanctum a Patre Filioque manantem tanquam ex uno principio, et eosdem nectentem, in corda nostra: id est, dona Spiritus Sancti ubique existentis, mentibus nostris infudit. Tunc enim Spiritus Sanctus dari et mitti asseritur, quum dona ejus gratifica conferuntur, sicut plenius dictum est supra. Clamantem, id est, nos fiducialiter clamare facientem ad Deum omnipotentem et trinum: O Abba (Pater). Duo nomina ista idem significant. Abba autem est nomen Hebraeum quod nomine patris exponitur. Itaque Spiritus Sanctus probat nos esse filios Dei. Nam ut probaremur adoptati a Deo in filios, Spiritum suum tribuit nobis in signum et arrham, ut ostendat affectum Patris in nos, detque fiduciam appellandi Deum, Patrem.
paras.en: Next the Apostle shows what follows in us from the divine adoption. [[4:6|And because you are|Quoniam autem estis]], O Galatians and all you faithful, [[4:6|sons|filii Dei]] of God by adoption, chosen from eternity, therefore, as a sign of this sonship, [[4:6|God hath sent|misit Deus]] the Father [[4:6|the Spirit of his Son|Spiritum Filii sui]], that is, the Holy Ghost, proceeding from the Father and the Son as from one principle and binding them together, [[4:6|into your hearts|in corda nostra]] [Denis reads "into our hearts"]: that is, He has poured into our minds the gifts of the Holy Ghost, who is everywhere. For the Holy Ghost is said to be given and sent when His gifts of grace are bestowed, as was said more fully above. [[4:6|crying|Clamantem]], that is, making us cry out with confidence to God almighty and three: O [[4:6|Abba, Father|Abba (Pater)]]. These two names mean the same thing: *Abba* is a Hebrew name, which is rendered by the name *father*. So the Holy Ghost proves us to be sons of God. For that we might be proved adopted by God as sons, He has given us His Spirit as a sign and a pledge, to show the Father's affection toward us and to give us confidence to call God Father.

paras.t: Ex his infert Apostolus: Itaque, id est, quoniam Spiritus Sanctus facit nos clamare, Abba (Pater), jam tempore evangelicæ legis, non est aliquis vere credentium, servus subjectus servitio timoris: de quo servo scriptum est, Servus non manet in domo in æternum; et alibi, Jam non dicam vos servos, sed amicos; sed filius est. Quod si filius Dei adoptivus est homo credens, sequitur quod et heres vitæ æternæ erit per Deum, id est a Deo, vel per misericordiam Dei. Unde dicitur: Filius manet in domo in æternum.
paras.en: From this the Apostle infers: [[4:7|Therefore|Itaque]], that is, since the Holy Ghost makes us cry, Abba (Father), [[4:7|now|jam]], in the time of the law of the Gospel, [[4:7|he is not|non est]] (no true believer is) [[4:7|a servant|servus]] subject to the servitude of fear, of which servant it is written: [[John 8:35|the servant abideth not in the house for ever|Servus non manet in domo in æternum]]; and elsewhere: [[John 15:15|I will not now call you servants|Jam non dicam vos servos]], [[John 15:15|But I have called you friends|sed amicos]] [Denis joins the two clauses of the verse]; [[4:7|but a son|sed filius est]]. [[4:7|And if a son|Quod si filius]] of God by adoption the believing man is, it follows that he will be [[4:7|an heir also|et heres]] of eternal life [[4:7|through God|per Deum]], that is, from God, or through the mercy of God. Hence it is said: [[John 8:35|the son abideth for ever|Filius manet in domo in æternum]] [Denis repeats "in the house" from the first half of the verse].

paras.t: Insuper, increpat ingratitudinem Galatarum. Sed tunc quidem, id est tempore gentilitatis vestræ, ignorantes Deum verum, his qui natura non sunt dii, sed vana hominum æstimatione, id est, qui veram deitatem non habent, serviebatis, videlicet idolis, et creaturis potius quam Creatori.
paras.en: Moreover, he rebukes the ingratitude of the Galatians. [[4:8|But then indeed|Sed tunc quidem]], that is, in the time of your heathenism, [[4:8|not knowing God|ignorantes Deum verum]] [Denis reads "the true God"], [[4:8|them who, by nature, are not gods|his qui natura non sunt dii]], but only in the vain opinion of men, that is, who have not true deity, [[4:8|you served|serviebatis]], namely idols, and [[Rom 1:25|the creature rather than the Creator|creaturis potius quam Creatori]].

paras.t: Nunc autem quum per meam prædicationem et Spiritus Sancti illustrationem cognoveritis Deum fide formata, quamdiu stetistis in gratia, imo cogniti sitis a Deo per approbationem, ad minus secundum præsentem justitiam quando in gratia statis; quomodo convertimini iterum, id est, a fide et cultu novæ legis reditis, ad infirma et egena elementa, id est præcepta legis cærimonialia? Quæ dicuntur elementa propter rationem prædictam. Dicuntur quoque infirma, quoniam non sufficiunt ad salutem; et egena, eo quod gratiam non continebant, nec justificabant. Sed quum Galatæ ante sui conversionem gentiles fuerint, nec unquam servaverint legem, quomodo dicit eis Apostolus, Convertimini iterum ad infirma et egena elementa, quibus denuo servire vultis? Respondet Hieronymus, quia tempore novæ legis, observantia cærimonialium idem seu par peccatum est cum idololatria.
paras.en: [[4:9|But now, after that|Nunc autem quum]] through my preaching and the enlightening of the Holy Ghost [[4:9|you have known God|cognoveritis Deum]] by formed faith [*fides formata*, faith quickened by charity], as long as you stood in grace, [[4:9|or rather are known by God|imo cogniti sitis a Deo]] by His approval, at least according to present justice, while you stand in grace: [[4:9|how turn you again|quomodo convertimini iterum]], that is, go back from the faith and worship of the new law, [[4:9|to the weak and needy elements|ad infirma et egena elementa]], that is, the ceremonial precepts of the law? They are called elements for the reason given above. They are called weak too, because they do not suffice for salvation; and needy, because they did not contain grace, nor did they justify. But since the Galatians were Gentiles before their conversion and had never kept the law, how does the Apostle say to them, [[4:9|turn you again to the weak and needy elements|Convertimini iterum ad infirma et egena elementa]], [[4:9|which you desire to serve again|quibus denuo servire vultis]]? Jerome answers that in the time of the new law the observance of the ceremonies is the same sin as idolatry, or an equal one.

paras.t: Dies, videlicet sabbata, dies azymorum et expiationum, observatis, id est, colitis atque attenditis more ac ritu Judæorum, et menses, id est neomenias, et mensem primum ac septimum, et tempora egressionis ex Ægypto, et annos, id est annum septimum remissionis, et quinquagesimum jubilæum. Quidam exponunt hæc de reditu ad idololatriam, et de superstitiosa observatione temporum, elementorum ac siderum, secundum quam aliqui dicunt: Tali tempore, die, seu anni initio, nihil est inchoandum, agendum, seu patiendum. Sed non videtur pertinere ad præsens. Non enim reprehenduntur Galatæ de reditu ad idololatriam, sed quod pseudoapostolis crediderunt: qui utique non idololatriam, sed legalia docuerunt.
paras.en: [[4:10|You observe|observatis]] [[4:10|days|Dies]], namely sabbaths and the days of unleavened bread and of expiation; that is, you keep them and attend to them after the manner and rite of the Jews; [[4:10|and months|et menses]], that is, new moons, and the first and the seventh month, [[4:10|and times|et tempora]] of the going out from Egypt, [[4:10|and years|et annos]], that is, the seventh year, of remission, and the fiftieth, the jubilee. Some expound these words of a return to idolatry and of the superstitious observance of times, elements and stars, according to which some say: At such a time, on such a day, or at the beginning of the year, nothing is to be begun, done or undergone. But this does not seem to belong to the present matter. For the Galatians are not rebuked for going back to idolatry, but for believing the false apostles, who certainly taught not idolatry but the legal observances.

paras.t: Timeo vos, id est de vobis, ut qui jam a Deo deviatis, ne forte sine causa, id est fructu et utilitate, laboraverim in vobis, prædicando, et alia bona ad vestri conversionem spectantia operando. Timeo namque ne penitus pereatis. Estote sicut ego, legalia dimittendo, sicut ego ea dimisi, quia et ego sum sine lege, sicut vos sine ea fuistis, et nunc esse debetis.
paras.en: [[4:11|I am afraid of you|Timeo vos]], that is, for you, as men already straying from God, [[4:11|lest perhaps|ne forte]] [[4:11|in vain|sine causa]], that is, without fruit and profit, [[4:11|I have laboured|laboraverim]] [[4:11|among you|in vobis]], by preaching and doing other good works bearing on your conversion. For I fear that you may perish utterly. [[4:12|Be ye as I|Estote sicut ego]], by leaving the legal observances, as I have left them, [[4:12|because I also am|quia et ego sum]] without the law, [[4:12|as you|sicut vos]] were without it, and ought to be now.

paras.t: Præterea sanctus Apostolus, more sapientissimi medici, post asperam correptionem adjungit dulcem et consolatoriam admonitionem; pristina quoque Galatarum bona commendat, ne consideratione præteritorum malorum desperent. Fratres, obsecro vos, id est, per sacra rogo, videlicet converti ad evangelicam veritatem. Et fiducialiter obsecro: nam nihil me læsistis, id est, in nullo me offendistis directe quoad personam meam, quamvis vehementissime doleam de hoc quod Deum offendistis, propriamque salutem negligitis. Scitis autem quia per infirmitatem carnis, id est cum magna corporis afflictione et persecutione, quam ab aliis passus fui antequam vobis prædicare incepi, evangelizavi vobis fidem Christi jampridem, id est, dudum quum apud vos eram. Et tentationem vestram vobis a dæmone infusam in carne mea, id est de afflictionibus corporis mei (tentavit enim eos diabolus, ne personæ tam abjectæ, ut videbatur esse Apostolus, tamque afflictæ, fidem adhiberent), non spreveristis neque respuistis, id est, non inadvertenter eam admisistis, nec parvi pendistis tentationem hanc dæmonis, sed digne restitistis. Sed sicut angelum Dei excepistis me, id est, cum ingenti reverentia personam meam tractastis, verba mea audistis, rationibus consensistis, imo sicut Christum Jesum me suscepistis, id est, tam caritative ac honorifice velut si Christus in propria persona visibiliter venisset ad vos, qui et ipse est magni consilii Angelus.
paras.en: Further, the holy Apostle, in the manner of a most wise physician, after a sharp rebuke adds a sweet and consoling admonition; he also commends the former good deeds of the Galatians, lest they despair in considering their past evils. [[4:12|brethren, I beseech you|Fratres, obsecro vos]], that is, I entreat you by holy things, namely to turn back to the truth of the Gospel.
