And I beseech you with confidence, for [[4:12|You have not injured me at all|nihil me læsistis]], that is, you have in nothing offended me directly as regards my own person, although I grieve most vehemently that you have offended God and neglect your own salvation. [[4:13|And you know how, through infirmity of the flesh|Scitis autem quia per infirmitatem carnis]], that is, with great affliction of body and with persecution, which I had suffered from others before I began to preach to you, [[4:13|I preached the gospel to you|evangelizavi vobis]] the faith of Christ [[4:13|heretofore|jampridem]], that is, some time ago, when I was among you. [[4:13|and your temptation|Et tentationem vestram]], put into you by the devil, [[4:13|in my flesh|in carne mea]], that is, concerning the afflictions of my body (for the devil tempted them not to give credence to a person so abject and so afflicted as the Apostle seemed to be), [[4:14|You despised not, nor rejected|non spreveristis neque respuistis]], that is, you did not heedlessly let it in, nor did you make light of this temptation of the devil, but you resisted it worthily. [[4:14|but received me as an angel of God|Sed sicut angelum Dei excepistis me]], that is, you treated my person with very great reverence, heard my words, assented to my reasons; nay, [[4:14|even as Christ Jesus|sicut Christum Jesum]] you received me, that is, as lovingly and honourably as if Christ had come to you visibly in His own person, who Himself also is the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [the margin gives Is. liv, 6, according to the Septuagint; the title "Angel of great counsel" is in the Septuagint of Is 9:6].

paras.t: Ubi est ergo beatitudo vestra? id est, quum olim tam virtuose egeritis, ubi est nunc meritum vestrum? tanquam dicat: Mirum est quod a tanta perfectione sic subito cadistis. Quod autem tam reverenter me suscepistis, jamque in spe beati fuistis, hinc patet: Testimonium enim perhibeo vobis, quia si fieri potuisset, id est licuisset, oportuisset, vel mihi expediens fuisset, oculos vestros, qui sunt membra carissima, eruissetis et dedissetis mihi, ex nimia caritate. Est autem consuetudo Scripturæ, ut dicatur non posse fieri, quod non fit juste.
paras.en: [[4:15|Where is then your blessedness?|Ubi est ergo beatitudo vestra?]] that is, since you once acted so virtuously, where now is your merit? As if to say: It is a wonder that you have fallen so suddenly from such perfection. And that you received me so reverently, and were already blessed in hope, is clear from this: [[4:15|For I bear you witness that, if it could be done|Testimonium enim perhibeo vobis, quia si fieri potuisset]], that is, had it been lawful, or needful, or expedient for me, [[4:15|you would have plucked out|eruissetis]] [[4:15|your own eyes|oculos vestros]], which are the dearest members, [[4:15|and would have given them to me|et dedissetis mihi]], out of your exceeding love. Now it is the custom of Scripture to say that a thing cannot be done which is not done justly.

paras.t: Ergo, id est, quum hæc ita se habeant, sequi videtur quod inimicus vobis factus sum, verum dicens vobis, id est ob hoc quod vos juste atque veraciter increpo et informo: nam aliam causam inimicandi mihi non habetis, quia in nullo offendi vos.
paras.en: [[4:16|then|Ergo]], that is, since these things are so, it seems to follow that I am [[4:16|become your enemy|inimicus vobis factus sum]], [[4:16|because I tell you the truth|verum dicens vobis]], that is, because I rebuke and instruct you justly and truthfully: for you have no other cause for being my enemies, since I have offended you in nothing.

paras.t: Æmulantur, id est diligunt, vos falsi non bene, id est non ordinate, sed carnaliter et perverse; sed excludere vos volunt a mea dilectione, ab evangelica veritate, a regno cœlesti, ut illos æmulemini, id est, sectemini et ametis præ nobis.
paras.en: [[4:17|They are zealous in your regard|Æmulantur]], that is, they love you (the false ones, that is, the false apostles), [[4:17|not well|non bene]], that is, not in due order, but carnally and perversely; [[4:17|but they would exclude you|sed excludere vos volunt]] from my love, from the truth of the Gospel, from the kingdom of heaven, [[4:17|that you might be zealous for them|ut illos æmulemini]], that is, that you might follow them and love them before us.

paras.t: Bonum autem, id est actum virtuosum seu hominem bonum, æmulamini, id est, amate atque sectamini, in bono, id est bona intentione, et propter finem bonum, seu propter ipsum bonum honestum in se, non propter utile aut delectabile: quoniam hæc est sola vera et sincera dilectio, quæ fundatur in bono honesto. Hoc autem facite semper, quia qui perseveraverit usque in finem, salvus erit; et non tantum quum præsens sum corporaliter apud vos, ne videamini bona agere potius mei timore sive intuitu, quam divino amore atque respectu. Decet enim subditos in absentia sui prælati diligentius custodire ea quæ Dei sunt et honestatem concernunt, quam in ejus præsentia, propter causam prædictam, et etiam quia tunc magis necessarium est, et est signum quod homo divino stimuletur amore.
paras.en: [[4:18|But be zealous for|æmulamini]], that is, love and follow, [[4:18|that which is good|Bonum autem]], that is, a virtuous act or a good man, [[4:18|in a good thing|in bono]], that is, with a good intention and for a good end, or for the sake of the good itself, the good that is honest in itself [*bonum honestum*, the good desirable for its own sake], not for the useful or the pleasant: for this alone is true and sincere love, which is founded on the honest good. And do this [[4:18|always|semper]], because [[Matt 10:22|he that shall persevere unto the end|qui perseveraverit usque in finem]], [[Matt 10:22|he shall be saved|salvus erit]]; [[4:18|and not only when I am present|et non tantum quum præsens sum]] in the body [[4:18|with you|apud vos]], lest you seem to do good out of fear or regard for me rather than out of divine love and respect. For it becomes subjects, in the absence of their prelate, to keep more diligently than in his presence the things that are God's and concern uprightness, for the reason given, and also because it is more necessary then, and it is a sign that a man is spurred on by divine love.

paras.t: Denique, declarata gravi conditione existentium sub lege, per humanæ consuetudinis exemplum, nunc idem declarat per legis divinam auctoritatem. Filioli mei, qui parvi estis in perfectione virtutum, quos iterum parturio, id est, cum dolore et planctu spiritualiter regenero, transferendo vos de non esse spirituali ad esse spirituale, per hujus epistolæ documenta, donec formetur, id est recipiatur ac describatur, Christus in vobis, id est in cordibus vestris per fidem puram, jugem memoriam, et dilectionem firmatam. Vellem autem apud vos esse modo corporali præsentia, si negotia paterentur, et mutare vocem meam, id est aliter vobis proprio ore loqui quam scribo, increpando vos durius quam scribere volo; quoniam confundor, id est, apud alios erubesco, in vobis, id est de vestri seductione.
paras.en: Lastly, having made plain the heavy condition of those who are under the law by an example from human custom, he now makes the same plain by the divine authority of the law. [[4:19|My little children|Filioli mei]], who are little in the perfection of virtues, [[4:19|of whom I am in labour again|quos iterum parturio]], that is, whom I regenerate spiritually with sorrow and lamentation, bringing you over from spiritual non-being to spiritual being, by the teaching of this epistle, [[4:19|until Christ be formed|donec formetur]], that is, be received and drawn, [[4:19|in you|Christus in vobis]], that is, in your hearts, by pure faith, constant remembrance and steadfast love. [[4:20|And I would willingly be present with you now|Vellem autem apud vos esse modo]] in bodily presence, if my affairs allowed, [[4:20|and change my voice|et mutare vocem meam]], that is, speak to you with my own mouth otherwise than I write, rebuking you more harshly than I am willing to write; [[4:20|because I am ashamed|quoniam confundor]], that is, I blush before others, [[4:20|for you|in vobis]], that is, because of your being led astray.

paras.t: Consequenter ostendit cessationem legalium per mysticam expositionem Scripturæ legalis. Dicite, id est respondete, mihi, qui sub lege vultis esse, id est cærimonialibus legis jussionibus obedire. Legem non legistis? id est, an libros veteris Testamenti legistis? tanquam dicat: Vel non legistis, vel male intellexistis. Ideo autem quæro, an legem legistis, an spiritualiter intellexistis:
paras.en: Next he shows the cessation of the legal ordinances by a mystical exposition of the Scripture of the law. [[4:21|Tell|Dicite]], that is, answer, [[4:21|me|mihi]], [[4:21|you that desire to be under the law|qui sub lege vultis esse]], that is, to obey the ceremonial commands of the law: [[4:21|have you not read the law?|Legem non legistis?]] that is, have you read the books of the Old Testament? As if to say: Either you have not read them, or you have understood them ill. And I ask whether you have read the law, whether you have understood it spiritually, for this reason:

paras.t: Scriptum est enim in libro Genesis, quoniam Abraham duos filios principales ac famosiores ceteris, utpote Isaac et Ismaelem, habuit. Habuit quoque alios multos post obitum Sarae, de Cetura. […]nit, videlicet Ismaelem, habuit […] Ægyptiaca Agar: quæ tamen erat antequam Abraham eam cognosceret […] abus tusset adulter; […] […]ac, habuit […] id est de Sara […] nunquam ancilla Abrahæ erat, qu[…] eam ex humilitate dominum appella[…] quantam illa fuit caritatis, non servi[…] subjecto […] produxit, […] Ismael […], id est […] lem eatus propagationem, fecundi[…] atque originem, sine miraculo, […] Poterat enim Abraham senex de juve[…] naturaliter generare […] gentes fuit, videlicet Isaac, […] id est ex promissione et repetit[…] promissione et miraculosa operatione […]fus est. Nam Sara sterilis fuit et ne[…] nata muliebribus carens. Unde […] virtute data est ei fecunditas; sæpius […] promissa fuit nativitas Isaac.
paras.en: [[4:22|For it is written|Scriptum est enim]] in the book of Genesis [[4:22|that Abraham had two sons|quoniam Abraham duos filios]], the principal ones and more famous than the rest, namely Isaac and Ismael. He also had many others, by Cetura, after the death of Sara[[Gen 25:1||]] [the margin's reference here is unreadable except "Gen."; Cetura is named at Gen 25:1]. [From here to the end of v. 25 the right-hand ends of the lines are lost, and only fragments survive:] […], namely Ismael, he had […] the Egyptian Agar: who nevertheless was, before Abraham knew her, […] [some words here cannot be made out] […]; […] he had […] that is, by Sara […] was never Abraham's handmaid, […] her lord out of humility […] how great charity she had, not […] subject […] brought forth […] Ismael […], that is, […] propagation, fruitful […] and origin, without a miracle […]. For Abraham, though old, could beget naturally of a young […] […] was, namely Isaac, […] that is, by promise and […] by promise and miraculous working […]. For Sara was barren and […], lacking the ways of women [cf. Gen 18:11]. Hence […] by […] power fruitfulness was given her[[Gen 21:2||]]; more than once […] the birth of Isaac was promised [the margin gives xxi, 2].

paras.t: Quæ sunt per allegoriam, id est […]cum significationem, […] id est […] ut ex sensu litterali detur intelligi[…] sit cœlestium. Allegoria etenim […] quid sit cœlestium. Duo sunt […] qu[…] Sara et Agar, seu de libera et ancill[…][…]rumque filiis, dicta sunt, sunt […] per generalem significationem, id est dest[…] […] Testamentum […], […] vetus Testamentum. In monte S[…]tam, ut patet in Exodo. Unde in l[…]roni uno legitur: Dominus de Sina […] Sina autem et Sinai idem significa[…] servitutem […] id est, hoc […] Testamentum Judæos servituti leg[…] subdidit, eosque timore pœnarum c[…] per temporalia promissa fecit Deo […]es, quæ servitus legalis seu timor[…] logitativus […] id est, per Agar an[…] Abraham designatur.
paras.en: [[4:24|Which things are said by an allegory|Quæ sunt per allegoriam]], that is, […] […] meaning, […] that is, […] so that from the literal sense it may be given to understand […] of heavenly things. For allegory […] what […] of heavenly things. Two are […] Sara and Agar, or of the free woman and the bondwoman and their sons, were said, are […] by a general meaning, that is, […] Testament […], […] the old Testament. On Mount S[…] […], as is plain in Exodus. Hence in […] [probably "in the book of Deuteronomy"] we read: The Lord from Sina […][[Deut 33:2||]] [the margin reads "xx"; the words are those of Deut 33:2, "The Lord came from Sinai"]. Now Sina and Sinai mean the same […] [[4:24|bondage|servitutem]] […] that is, this […] Testament subjected the Jews to the servitude of the law […], and by fear of punishments […] by temporal promises made […] to God […], which legal servitude or fear […] […] that is, by Agar the handmaid […] of Abraham is signified.

paras.t: Sina […] […] Sina […]tur) sua magnitudine diversas tangi[…] vinclas, et in sua extremitate fertur[…] promissorum vilibus; quæ mons Sin[…] continuus; non loco sed allegorico[…] lecto, […] quæ sunt ambulantes […] terrenæ præsentique Synagogæ; qu[…] […]pore Pauli in Jerusalem fuit. Significat enim hanc plebem, ejusque servitutem. Servitus autem legis per montem Sina signata, tunc vigebat in Jerusalem, in qua legalia et sacrificia servabantur. Et servit cum filiis suis, id est synagoga Judæorum cum personis sibi subjectis servit Domino servili timore, ut patuit.
paras.en: Sina […] […] Sina […]) by its size touches various […] [perhaps "provinces"], and at its far end is borne […] of the promises […]; which mountain Sina […] adjoining; not in place but allegorically understood, […] who are walking […] to the earthly and present Synagogue, which […] in the time of Paul was in Jerusalem. For it signifies this people and its servitude. For the servitude of the law, signified by Mount Sina, was then in force in Jerusalem, in which the legal ordinances and sacrifices were kept. [[4:25|and is in bondage with her children|Et servit cum filiis suis]], that is, the synagogue of the Jews, with the persons subject to it, serves the Lord with servile fear, as has been shown.

paras.t: Illa autem quæ sursum est Jerusalem, id est Ecclesia militans, ex gentibus maxime congregata: quæ dicitur sursum, quia per contemplationem et spem atque divinum amorem, ad divina erigitur, jamque per inchoationem angelicæ conversationis in cœlestibus demoratur; libera est a servitute peccati et conditione servili, seu observantia legis. Quæ Ecclesia est […] mater nostra. In Baptismo enim ex ea et Spiritu Sancto renascimur.
paras.en: [[4:26|But that Jerusalem which is above|Illa autem quæ sursum est Jerusalem]], that is, the Church militant, gathered chiefly from the Gentiles, which is said to be above because by contemplation, hope and divine love it is raised up to divine things, and by a beginning of the angelic way of life already dwells in heavenly things, [[4:26|is free|libera est]] from the servitude of sin and from the servile condition, or the observance of the law. This Church is […] [[4:26|our mother|mater nostra]]. For in Baptism we are born again of her and of the Holy Ghost.

paras.t: Denique, quod sit mater nostra, ostendit auctoritate prophetica. Scriptum est enim in Isaia: Lætare sterilis quæ non paris, id est, collectio gentium, quæ tempore Testamenti veteris fuerat infecunda et dolorum dedita; erumpe et clama, qui non parturis: id est, ex interioris lætitiæ magnitudine in exteriorem exsultationem, laudem vocalem et gratiarum actionem prorumpe. Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur. Propter quod ait Psalmista: Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum (Ps. lxxxiii, 3). Quia plures sunt filii Ecclesiæ ex gentibus adunatæ, quæ olim erat a Deo relicta, magis quam synagoga, quæ habuit sponsum cœlestem, videlicet Deum, cui in legis susceptione fuerat desponsata. Certum est enim Ecclesiam numero et merito excedere Synagogam.
paras.en: Lastly, he shows by the authority of prophecy that she is our mother. [[4:27|For it is written|Scriptum est enim]] in Isaias[[Is 54:1||]]: [[4:27|Rejoice, thou barren, that bearest not|Lætare sterilis quæ non paris]], that is, the assembly of the Gentiles, which in the time of the Old Testament had been unfruitful and given over to sorrows; [[4:27|break forth and cry thou that travailest not|erumpe et clama, qui non parturis]]: that is, out of the greatness of inward joy break forth into outward exultation, vocal praise and thanksgiving. For [[Matt 12:34|out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh|Ex abundantia enim cordis os loquitur]]. Wherefore the Psalmist says: [[Ps 83:3|My heart and my flesh have rejoiced in the living God|Cor meum et caro mea exsultaverunt in Deum vivum]] (Ps. lxxxiii, 3). For the children of the Church gathered from the Gentiles, which was once forsaken by God, are many, [[4:27|more than|magis quam]] of the synagogue, which had a heavenly bridegroom, namely God, to whom she had been espoused in receiving the law. For it is certain that the Church exceeds the Synagogue in number and in merit.

paras.t: Vos autem Christifideles, o fratres, juxta typum et simul traditionem Isaac, […] id est coelestis benedictionis et spiritualis generationis, […] quia ex aqua et Spiritu Sancto renascimur, gratiamque cœlestis beatitudinis obtinemus. Sic ergo per Isaac designatur Ecclesia Christi.
paras.en: But you faithful of Christ, O [[4:28|brethren|fratres]], according to the type and also the handing down of Isaac, […] [the words of the verse seem to be lost here], that is, of the heavenly blessing and of spiritual generation, […] because we are born again of water and the Holy Ghost, and obtain the grace of heavenly beatitude. Thus, then, the Church of Christ is signified by Isaac.

paras.t: Sed quemadmodum tunc, scilicet tempore […] Abraham […] id est per repromissionem […] ludum Hebræi intelligunt, quod c[…]erit Ismael fratrem suum Isaac […] et nunc, scilicet tempore Pauli ap[…] carnales Judæi, pseudoapostoli, tyra[…]que hæretici, secundum carnem e[…]guinibus nati, persequuntur fideles […] natos, in quibus permanet semen […] est verbum seu gratia Christi. Omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo, po[…] […]
paras.en: [[4:29|But as then|Sed quemadmodum tunc]], namely in the time of […] Abraham […] that is, by promise […] [several lines are lost here] […] by "play" the Hebrews understand that Ismael […] his brother Isaac […] [two more lines are lost]. [[4:29|so also it is now|et nunc]], namely in the time of the apostle Paul [the last word is partly lost], the carnal Jews, the false apostles, tyrants and heretics, born according to the flesh, of blood [the word is partly lost], persecute the faithful […] born, in whom remains the seed […] is the word or grace of Christ. [[2 Tim 3:12|all that will live godly in Christ|Omnes qui volunt pie vivere in Christo]] [the margin gives II Tim. iii; the words are those of 2 Tim 3:12] […] […]

paras.t: […]secutionem justorum ab impiis, pon[…]stolus consolationem idoneam. Se[…] […] sunt verba ad Abraham. Quæ quum […]set Ismaelem cum Isaac dolose ludo[…] […] nostra expelle, ancillam hanc Agar […] […]maelem filium ejus: non enim her[…] […] litteram. Per quod spiritualiter fig[…]tur, quod Synagoga atque legalis […]vantia essent tempore evangelicæ […] a populo christiano separandæ conversatione, loco et merito, et postmodum præmio.
paras.en: […] persecution of the just by the wicked, the Apostle […] a fitting consolation. Se[…] [the words of v. 30 are lost here] […] [a line or more is lost] […] are words to Abraham. When she […] Ismael […] deceitfully with Isaac […] our […], cast out this handmaid Agar […] Ismael her son: for […] not […] heir […] [these are Sara's words, Gen 21:10] […] the letter. By which it is spiritually signified that the Synagogue and the legal observance were, in the time of the Gospel […], to be separated from the Christian people in conduct, place and merit, and afterwards in reward [the end of this sentence stands at the head of the next column, PDF 307].

5.note: The printed title of this article is lost in the transcription. The article opens with Gal 4:31.

paras.t: Itaque, fratres, non sumus ancillæ, id est veteris Testamenti Synagogæ, seu legalis observantiæ, filii, sed liberæ, id est militantis Ecclesiæ et libertatis christianæ; qua libertate, id est per cujus libertatis communicationem seu infusionem, Christus nos liberavit formaliter, sicut per gratiam salvat. Liberavit, inquam, nos ab onere legis, a jugo peccati, et dæmonis dominio. Unde per evangelistam Joannem Dominus dicit: Si Filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis. Hæc ergo libertas, secundum Glossam, est peccatorum remissio, et fidei per dilectionem operantis justificatio. Vel sic: Sumus filii liberæ, id est Ecclesiæ, libertate dilectionis, ut sponte, hilariter et caritative, non serviliter, formidolose et coacte obediamus Ecclesiæ, et Domino ministremus: qua libertate in anima Christi existente, liberavit nos Christus efficienter propria passione. Christus enim mera caritate, atque spontanea libertate ad caritatem pertinente, pro nobis mori dignatus est, juxta illud Isaiæ: Oblatus est quia ipse voluit. Unde et passione instante dixit ad Petrum: An putas quia non possum rogare Patrem meum, […] decem legiones angelorum?
paras.en: [[Gal 4:31|So then, brethren, we are not the children of the bondwoman|Itaque, fratres, non sumus ancillæ]], that is, of the Synagogue of the Old Testament, or of the observance of the law, [[Gal 4:31|but of the free|filii, sed liberæ]], that is, of the Church militant and of Christian freedom: [[Gal 4:31|by the freedom wherewith|qua libertate]], that is, by the communication or infusion of which freedom, [[Gal 4:31|Christ has made us free|Christus nos liberavit]] formally [that is, freedom is the form, in the soul, by which he frees us], as he saves by grace. He has made us free, I say, from the burden of the law, from the yoke of sin, and from the dominion of the devil. Hence the Lord says by the evangelist John: [[John 8:36|If|Si]] [[John 8:36|the son shall make you free, you shall be free indeed|Filius vos liberaverit, vere liberi eritis]]. This freedom, then, according to the Gloss, is the remission of sins and the justification of faith that worketh by charity. Or thus: we are children [[Gal 4:31|of the free|liberæ]], that is, of the Church, by the freedom of love, so that we obey the Church and serve the Lord willingly, cheerfully and with charity, not servilely, fearfully and under compulsion: [[Gal 4:31|by the freedom wherewith|qua libertate]], existing in the soul of Christ, [[Gal 4:31|Christ has made us free|liberavit nos Christus]] efficiently [that is, as the agent who brings it about] by his own passion. For Christ, out of pure charity, and with the spontaneous freedom that belongs to charity, deigned to die for us, according to that of Isaias: [[Is 53:7|He was offered because it was his own will|Oblatus est quia ipse voluit]] [the margin gives Joan. xviii, 7; the words are Isaias 53:7]. Hence also, as his passion drew near, he said to Peter: [[Matt 26:53|Thinkest thou that I cannot ask my Father|An putas quia non possum rogare Patrem meum]], […] ten [[Matt 26:53|legions of angels|legiones angelorum]]? [a line of the text is lost here; the text as it stands reads *decem*, "ten", where the Gospel has "twelve", *duodecim*]

paras.t: […] legalium jussione, contineri, id est con[…]
paras.en: […] by the bidding of the legal ordinances, [[5:1|held|contineri]], that is, con[…] [the opening words of verse 1 and Denis's gloss on them are lost in the source, before and after these words]

paras.t: […] rapto, secure et absolute credendum est, dico vobis: quoniam si circumcidamini more Judaico, Christus vobis nihil proderit, id est, ex fide, passione et merito Christi nullum consequemini fructum, propter vestram perversitatem, quemadmodum medicus optimus nihil prodest rebelli infirmo.
paras.en: […] caught up, must be believed securely and absolutely [the beginning of this sentence, with the first words of verse 2, "Behold, I Paul", is lost in the source; *rapto*, "caught up", seems to refer to Paul], [[5:2|tell you, that if you be circumcised|dico vobis: quoniam si circumcidamini]] after the Jewish manner, [[5:2|Christ shall profit you nothing|Christus vobis nihil proderit]]: that is, you will obtain no fruit from faith in Christ, from his passion and merit, because of your perversity, just as the best physician profits nothing a rebellious patient.

paras.t: Testificor autem rursus, id est, firmiter assero, omni homini, sive Judæo, sive gentili, circumcidenti se, quasi circumcisio necessaria sit ad salutem, quoniam debitor est universæ legis faciendæ, id est, circumcisionem accipiendo, obligat se ad universa quæ præcipiuntur in lege, videlicet ad observantiam præceptorum moralium, cærimonialium ac judicialium. Quemadmodum enim Baptismum suscipiens, obligat se ad præcepta Evangelii; sic circumcisionem accipiens, ad universa legis mandata tenetur, ita ut tantum teneatur ad alia, sicut ad circumcisionem: quamvis absolute nec ad hanc, nec ad totam legem observandam sit obligatus; sed circumcisionem accipiendo, ostendit ipso facto quod se ad omnia obliget.
paras.en: [[5:3|And I testify again|Testificor autem rursus]], that is, I firmly assert, [[5:3|to every man|omni homini]], whether Jew or gentile, [[5:3|circumcising himself|circumcidenti se]], as if circumcision were necessary to salvation, [[5:3|that he is a debtor to do the whole law|quoniam debitor est universæ legis faciendæ]]: that is, by receiving circumcision he binds himself to everything that is commanded in the law, namely to the observance of the moral, ceremonial and judicial precepts. For as one who receives Baptism binds himself to the precepts of the Gospel, so one who receives circumcision is held to all the commandments of the law, so that he is held to the others as much as to circumcision; although, absolutely speaking, he is not obliged either to this or to keeping the whole law, yet by receiving circumcision he shows by the very fact that he binds himself to all.

paras.t: Evacuati estis a Christo, id est, a participatione virtutum beneficiorumque Christi inanes effecti estis, legalia recipiendo, qui in lege justificamini, id est, per observationem legis Mosaicæ justificari optatis aut creditis; a gratia, id est gratuita justificatione per fidem Christi, imo ab ipso habitu gratiæ, excidistis, peccando tam graviter.
paras.en: [[5:4|You are made void of Christ|Evacuati estis a Christo]], that is, you have been made empty of any share in the virtues and benefits of Christ by taking up the legal observances, [[5:4|you who are justified in the law|qui in lege justificamini]], that is, who wish or believe to be justified by observing the law of Moses: [[5:4|from grace|a gratia]], that is, from the free justification through faith in Christ, nay, from the very habit of grace [that is, grace as an abiding quality of the soul], [[5:4|you are fallen|excidistis]], by sinning so grievously.

paras.t: Quod autem hoc ita sit, patet ex contrario. Nos enim Apostoli primitias Spiritus habentes, et omnes veraciter christiani, spiritu, id est Spiritus Sancti instinctu, seu spirituali intellectu, ex fide Christi, spem justitiæ, id est speratam justitiam, seu plenum justitiæ præmium, scilicet vitam æternam, exspectamus, quia per fidem et gratiam sine operibus legis salvari speramus. Sæpe autem in Scripturis sumitur spes pro re sperata.
paras.en: That this is so is plain from the contrary. [[5:5|For we|Nos enim]] Apostles, [[Rom 8:23|who have the firstfruits of the Spirit|primitias Spiritus habentes]], and all who are truly Christians, [[5:5|in spirit|spiritu]], that is, by the prompting of the Holy Ghost, or by spiritual understanding, [[5:5|by faith|ex fide]] in Christ, [[5:5|wait|exspectamus]] [[5:5|for the hope of justice|spem justitiæ]], that is, for the justice hoped for, or the full reward of justice, namely eternal life; for we hope to be saved through faith and grace without the works of the law. Now in the Scriptures *hope* is often taken for the thing hoped for.

paras.t: Merito autem sic exspectamus: Nam in Christo Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet ad salutem, tempore Evangelii divulgati, neque præputium, id est ritus gentilitatis: utrumque enim æqualiter reputatur inane, tempore novæ legis; sed fides quæ per dilectionem operatur implendo divina præcepta, aliquid valet, et sufficit ad salutem. Porro fides sine caritate informis est, et sine operibus mortua est, si tamen opportunitas operandi occurrat. Ad minus tamen in adultis exigitur actus interior caritatis et fidei ad salutem, quoniam arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur.
paras.en: And rightly do we so wait: [[5:6|For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing|Nam in Christo Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet]] unto salvation, in the time of the Gospel made known, [[5:6|nor uncircumcision|neque præputium]], that is, the rite of the gentiles: for both are reckoned equally void in the time of the new law; [[5:6|but faith that worketh by Charity|sed fides quæ per dilectionem operatur]], by fulfilling the divine precepts, availeth something and suffices for salvation. Moreover faith without charity is unformed [that is, lacking the charity that gives it life and merit], and [[Jas 2:20|without works is dead|sine operibus mortua est]], provided, however, that there is opportunity for working. At the least, however, an inward act of charity and of faith is required in adults for salvation, since every [[Matt 7:19|tree that bringeth not forth good fruit, shall be cut down|arbor quæ non facit fructum bonum, excidetur]][[Matt 3:10||]].

paras.t: Currebatis bene, o Galatæ, id est, festinanter et recto itinere processistis de via ad patriam, de exsilio isto ad paradisum cœlestem, de mediis ad ultimum finem, ita ut dicere potuissetis illud Psalmistæ: Viam mandatorum tuorum cucurri. Hic autem cursus est fervens desiderium mentis ad Deum, efficax quoque exsecutio cœlestium præceptorum. Quis vos impedivit ab isto cursu, veritati non obedire, id est, ut nostræ veræ prædicationi evangelicæque doctrinæ non obediatis. Nemini vos ab hac obedientia impedienti consenseritis.
paras.en: [[5:7|You did run well|Currebatis bene]], O Galatians, that is, you went forward swiftly and by the right road, from the way to the fatherland, from this exile to the heavenly paradise, from the means to the last end, so that you could have said that of the Psalmist: [[Ps 118:32|I have run the way of thy commandments|Viam mandatorum tuorum cucurri]]. Now this running is the fervent desire of the mind towards God, and also the effective carrying out of the heavenly precepts. [[5:7|What hath hindered you|Quis vos impedivit]] in that course, [[5:7|that you should not obey the truth|veritati non obedire]], that is, that you should not obey our true preaching and the gospel teaching? Consent to no one who would hinder you from this obedience [these words are printed in italics as if part of the text, but are not in the Clementine Vulgate or the Douay-Rheims; some old Latin copies read here *nemini consenseritis*, "consent to no one"].

paras.t: Persuasio hæc, id est topica argumentatio illorum qua vos ad legalia observanda nituntur inducere, non est, quantum ad suam falsitatem ac deformitatem, ex eo qui vocat vos, id est ex Deo, qui vos per inspirationem internam et nostram prædicationem vocat ad fidei sinceritatem et vitam æternam.
paras.en: [[5:8|This persuasion|Persuasio hæc]], that is, the topical argument [that is, an argument from probable grounds, not a demonstration] of those men, by which they strive to lead you to observe the legal ordinances, [[5:8|is not|non est]], as regards its falsehood and deformity, [[5:8|from him that calleth you|ex eo qui vocat vos]], that is, from God, who by inward inspiration and by our preaching calls you to the sincerity of faith and to eternal life.

paras.t: Modicum fermentum totam massam corrumpit. Hoc ad litteram ita est: quod in epistola ad Corinthios plenius est expositum. Quo significatur, quod pauci pestiferi, fallaces et indurati, totam fidelium congregationem inficiunt, ideo sunt vitandi.
paras.en: [[5:9|A little leaven corrupteth the whole lump|Modicum fermentum totam massam corrumpit]]. This is so in the letter, as has been set out more fully in the epistle to the Corinthians[[1 Cor 5:6||]]. By it is signified that a few pestilent, deceitful and hardened men infect the whole congregation of the faithful; therefore they are to be avoided.

paras.t: Ego autem confido in vobis, id est de vobis, in Domino, id est, quoniam ante virtutibus fuistis tam insignes, spero nunc quod resipiscetis a vestro errore, ita quod nihil aliud sapietis, perlecta ista epistola, nisi quod ego vos docui. Qui autem conturbat vos, id est, pacem et quietem mentis vestræ, quam in evangelica veritate habuistis, sollicitat et subvertit, portabit judicium reprobationis, id est, debitam pœnam sustinebit, nisi pœniteat, quicumque est ille, sive sit magnus, sive mediocris. Deus enim nil mali impunitum relinquit, juxta illud Job: Deus inultum abire non patitur.
paras.en: [[5:10|I have confidence in you|Ego autem confido in vobis]], that is, concerning you, [[5:10|in the Lord|in Domino]]: that is, since you were formerly so distinguished in virtues, I hope now that you will come to your senses from your error, so [[5:10|that you will not be of another mind|quod nihil aliud sapietis]], once this epistle has been read through, than what I taught you. [[5:10|but he that troubleth you|Qui autem conturbat vos]], that is, who unsettles and overthrows the peace and quiet of your mind which you had in the gospel truth, [[5:10|shall bear the judgment|portabit judicium]] of reprobation, that is, shall undergo the punishment due, unless he repent, [[5:10|whosoever he be|quicumque est ille]], whether he be great or of middling rank. For God leaves no evil unpunished, according to that of Job: [[Job 24:12|God doth not suffer it to pass unrevenged|Deus inultum abire non patitur]] [the margin gives Job xx, 12; the words are Job 24:12].

paras.t: Ego autem, fratres, si circumcisionem adhuc prædico observandam, ut mihi a pseudoapostolis illis imponitur: qui, ut facilius Galatas ad legalium observationes inducerent, asseruerunt Paulum apud alios adhuc circumcisionem prædicare. Si ergo hoc ago, quid, id est qua ratione, adhuc persecutionem patior a Judæis? Tanquam dicat, Nulla. Ob hoc quippe præcipue indignabantur et pœnas intulerunt Judæi Apostolo, quia cessationem circumcisionis ac sabbati docuit. Unde si circumcisionem adhuc prædicasset in gentibus, cessassent Judæi persequi ipsum. Ergo, id est, si circumcisionem doceo observandam, evacuatum, id est ablatum, est scandalum crucis, id est offendiculum passivum, seu scandalizatio Judæorum, quo irascuntur. Offenduntur seu scandalizantur de hoc, quod gloriam crucis prædicamus, asserentes ad salutem sufficere fidem et gratiam dominicæ passionis, magisque constare salutem in cruce quam in circumcisione. Si itaque Paulus circumcisionem docuisset, ut falsi illi dixerunt, non fuissent Judæi sic concitati adversus eum. Et quoniam Galatis innotuit Judæos persequi Paulum et scandalizari in prædicatione ipsius, idcirco per hæc innuit eis Apostolus falsum esse quod sibi imponebatur a perversis.
paras.en: [[5:11|And I, brethren, if I yet preach circumcision|Ego autem, fratres, si circumcisionem adhuc prædico]] as something to be observed, as is laid to my charge by those false apostles, who, to lead the Galatians the more easily to the observances of the law, asserted that Paul was still preaching circumcision among others. If then I do this, [[5:11|why|quid]], that is, for what reason, [[5:11|do I yet suffer persecution|adhuc persecutionem patior]] from the Jews? As if to say: for none. For it was chiefly for this that the Jews were indignant with the Apostle and inflicted punishments on him, that he taught that circumcision and the sabbath had ceased[[Acts 15:1||]][[Acts 15:2||]]. Hence, if he had still been preaching circumcision among the gentiles, the Jews would have ceased to persecute him. [[5:11|Then|Ergo]], that is, if I teach that circumcision is to be observed, [[5:11|is the scandal of the cross|est scandalum crucis]] [[5:11|made void|evacuatum]], that is, taken away: the scandal, that is, the passive stumbling-block [that is, offence taken by others, not given], or the scandalizing of the Jews, at which they grow angry. They are offended or scandalized at this, that we preach the glory of the cross, asserting that faith and the grace of the Lord's passion suffice for salvation, and that salvation stands in the cross rather than in circumcision. If then Paul had taught circumcision, as those false men said, the Jews would not have been so stirred up against him. And since it was known to the Galatians that the Jews were persecuting Paul and were scandalized at his preaching, by these words the Apostle intimates to them that what perverse men laid to his charge was false.

paras.t: Utinam et abscindantur, id est, a societate fidelium et vestro conventu penitus removeantur, imo et desistant, quantum ad culpam, qui vos conturbant, ingerendo auribus vestris falsam doctrinam, et inquietantes cor vestrum.
paras.en: [[5:12|I would they were even cut off|Utinam et abscindantur]], that is, wholly removed from the society of the faithful and from your assembly, nay, that they would also desist, as regards their guilt, [[5:12|who trouble you|qui vos conturbant]] by thrusting false doctrine into your ears and disquieting your heart.

paras.t: Vos enim in libertatem, id est exoneratione a servitute legalium; vel, in libertatem, id est evangelicam legem, quæ a Jacobo vocatur lex perfectæ libertatis, quoniam a servitute peccati ac dæmonum salvat; vel, in libertatem caritatis; vocati estis fratres, per gratiam Christi, qui nos a jugo legis absolvit, ut non timore, sed amore moveamur ad cultum divinum.
paras.en: [[5:13|For you|Vos enim]] [[5:13|unto liberty|in libertatem]], that is, unto release from the servitude of the legal observances; or, [[5:13|unto liberty|in libertatem]], that is, unto the gospel law, which is called by James [[Jas 1:25|the perfect law of liberty|lex perfectæ libertatis]], because it saves from the servitude of sin and of the devils; or, [[5:13|unto liberty|in libertatem]] of charity, [[5:13|brethren, have been called|vocati estis fratres]] by the grace of Christ, who has released us from the yoke of the law, so that we are moved to the worship of God not by fear but by love.

paras.t: Verumtamen, quoniam non est libertate hac abutendum, subjungitur: Tantum, id est, hoc solum vos precor ac moneo, ne libertatem vobis collatam in occasionem carnis detis, id est, ad satisfaciendum carnalibus concupiscentiis expendatis. Libertas nempe multis peccandi occasio est, quoniam pœnam non metuunt. Nam et hæretici quidam fuerunt, qui sibi per spiritus libertatem omnia licere asseruerunt: qui utique omnium vitiorum miserrimæ servituti subjecti fuerunt. Sed per caritatem divinam atque fraternam servite invicem, id est, ex dilectione interna ac pura procedite ad caritativa obsequia, mutuo succurrendo in spiritualibus ac temporalibus prout perfecta caritas (quæ omnia facit communia) exigit.
paras.en: But since this liberty is not to be abused, he adds: [[5:13|Only|Tantum]], that is, this alone I beg and warn you, [[5:13|make not liberty|ne libertatem]] bestowed on you [[5:13|an occasion to the flesh|in occasionem carnis]], that is, do not spend it on satisfying carnal concupiscences. For liberty is to many an occasion of sinning, because they do not fear punishment. For there were even certain heretics who asserted that through the liberty of the spirit all things were lawful to them: who were indeed subject to the most wretched servitude of all the vices. [[5:13|But by charity|Sed per caritatem]], divine and fraternal, [[5:13|serve one another|servite invicem]], that is, out of inward and pure love go forth to charitable services, helping one another in spiritual and temporal things, as perfect charity (which makes all things common) requires.

paras.t: Omnis enim lex, id est universa legis præcepta, in uno sermone impletur, id est, per observationem unius præcepti custodiantur. De quo sermone præceptivo subjungitur: Diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum, id est spiritualiter et propter Deum, in Deo, et in ordine ad vitam æternam. Licet enim duo sint caritatis præcepta propter materialem distinctionem objecti, de quibus ait Salvator, In his duobus mandatis tota lex pendet et Prophetæ; una tamen est caritas, qua Deus proximusque diligitur. Ideo hoc loco et alibi sæpe unum mandatum in alio includitur. Unde quum in dilectione proximi dicitur lex impleri, in dilectione proximi comprehenditur dilectio Dei. Porro verbum hoc, Diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum, in Levitico habetur.
paras.en: [[5:14|For all the law|Omnis enim lex]], that is, all the precepts of the law, [[5:14|is fulfilled in one word|in uno sermone impletur]], that is, they are kept by observing one precept. Of which preceptive word he adds: [[5:14|Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself|Diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum]], that is, spiritually and for God's sake, in God, and in order to eternal life. For although there are two precepts of charity, because of the material distinction of the object [that is, because they bear on two different things, God and neighbour], of which the Saviour says, [[Matt 22:40|On these two commandments dependeth the whole law and the prophets|In his duobus mandatis tota lex pendet et Prophetæ]], yet charity is one, by which God and neighbour are loved. Therefore here and often elsewhere one commandment is included in the other. Hence, when the law is said to be fulfilled in the love of neighbour, the love of God is comprehended in the love of neighbour. Further, this saying, [[5:14|Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself|Diliges proximum tuum sicut te ipsum]], is found in Leviticus[[Lev 19:18||]].

paras.t: Quod si invicem mordetis verbis pungitivis et pessimis, et comeditis, id est, fraudatis et devoratis, temporalia vel spiritualia bona vestra mutuo corrumpendo; videte, id est attendite, ne ab invicem consumamini, id est, penitus pereatis in anima et corpore. Tanquam dicat: Nisi a morsu invidiæ et mutua corrosione ac nocumento abstinueritis, anima vestra et corpus, omne esse spirituale atque gratificum perdet in sæculo isto, pœnasque æternas sentiet in inferno.
paras.en: [[5:15|But if you bite|Quod si invicem mordetis]] one another with stinging and most evil words, [[5:15|and devour|et comeditis]], that is, defraud and devour, corrupting one another's temporal or spiritual goods; [[5:15|take heed|videte]], that is, attend, [[5:15|you be not consumed one of another|ne ab invicem consumamini]], that is, that you perish utterly in soul and body. As if to say: Unless you abstain from the bite of envy and from gnawing and harming one another, your soul and body will lose all spiritual being and all being in grace in this world, and will feel eternal punishments in hell.

paras.t: Dico autem, id est, admoneo vos, in Christo, id est secundum Christi doctrinam: Spiritu ambulate: id est, secundum Spiritus Sancti instinctum agite. Vel, per spiritum designatur ratio, cujus judicium in omnibus sequi debemus: quoniam optimum hominis est esse secundum rationem, ut Dionysius protestatur. Et desideria carnis non perficietis, id est, carnales concupiscentias non deducetis ad effectum, neque præbebitis eis consensum, qui coram Deo pro opere reputatur.
paras.en: [[5:16|I say then|Dico autem]], that is, I admonish you, in Christ [printed in italics as part of the text, though not in the Clementine Vulgate], that is, according to the teaching of Christ: [[5:16|Walk in the spirit|Spiritu ambulate]], that is, act according to the prompting of the Holy Ghost. Or, by *spirit* reason is meant, whose judgment we ought to follow in all things, since man's best is to be according to reason, as Dionysius testifies. [[5:16|and you shall not fulfill the lusts of the flesh|Et desideria carnis non perficietis]], that is, you will not carry carnal concupiscences into effect, nor give them consent, which before God is reckoned as the deed.

paras.t: Caro enim, id est appetitus sensitivus, seu anima secundum carnem, vel ipse homo ex parte sensualitatis, concupiscit adversus spiritum, id est, ea desiderat quæ directe sunt rationi contraria, videlicet delectationes sensibiles, de quibus scriptum est: Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere. Spiritus autem, id est appetitus intellectualis, seu ratio, vel anima secundum partem sui superiorem, concupiscit adversus carnem, id est ea quæ carni et sensualitati laborem et tædium ingerunt, utpote spiritualia bona, continentiam, sobrietatem, divinorum frequentem ac stabilem vacationem, quibus caro castigatur, fatigatur et attenuatur. Hæc enim, videlicet caro et spiritus, sibi invicem adversantur, appetendo contraria, ut dictum est. Caro quippe cupit bona delectabilia et utilia, etiam inordinate seu ultra necessitatem; spiritus autem vult bona honesta per respectum ad Deum. Ut non quæcumque vultis, secundum rationis judicium, illa faciatis, propter sensualitatis rebellionem, quemadmodum alibi dicit Apostolus: Non quod volo bonum, hoc facio.
paras.en: [[5:17|For the flesh|Caro enim]], that is, the sensitive appetite, or the soul according to the flesh, or the man himself on the side of sensuality, [[5:17|lusteth against the spirit|concupiscit adversus spiritum]], that is, desires those things which are directly contrary to reason, namely sensible delights, of which it is written: [[Ecclus 18:30|Go not after thy lusts, but turn away from thy own will.|Post concupiscentias tuas non eas, et a voluntate tua avertere.]] [[5:17|And the spirit|Spiritus autem]], that is, the intellectual appetite, or reason, or the soul according to its higher part, lusts [[5:17|against the flesh|adversus carnem]], that is, for those things which bring labour and weariness to the flesh and the sensuality, such as spiritual goods, continence, sobriety, frequent and steady leisure for divine things, by which the flesh is chastised, wearied and made lean. [[5:17|For these|Hæc enim]], namely the flesh and the spirit, [[5:17|are contrary one to another|sibi invicem adversantur]], by desiring contrary things, as has been said. For the flesh craves delightful and useful goods, even inordinately or beyond necessity; but the spirit wills goods that are honest [*honesta*, that is, morally good in themselves] with regard to God. [[5:17|So that you do not|Ut non]] [[5:17|the things that you would|quæcumque vultis]] according to the judgment of reason, because of the rebellion of sensuality, as the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Rom 7:19|the good which I will, I do not|Non quod volo bonum, hoc facio]][[Rom 7:15||]].

paras.t: Vel sic sibi hæc adversantur, ut non quæcumque vultis, id est non omnia ad quæ inclinationem habetis, faciatis, sed per rationem vitia carnis refrenetis. Sicque dictio illa, Ut, tenetur concomitanter: quia ex illa mutua adversatione sequitur, ut non liceat nobis omnia operari quæ volumus. Hinc etiam testatur Petrus: Carissimi, inquiens, obsecro vos abstinere a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam.
paras.en: Or thus these are contrary one to another, [[5:17|so that you do not|ut non]] [[5:17|the things that you would|quæcumque vultis]], that is, not all the things to which you have an inclination, but restrain the vices of the flesh by reason. And so that word *so that* [*ut*] is taken concomitantly [that is, as marking what follows along with the conflict, not a purpose]: because from that mutual opposition it follows that it is not lawful for us to do all that we will. Hence also Peter testifies: [[1 Pet 2:11|Dearly beloved|Carissimi]], says he, [[1 Pet 2:11|I beseech you|obsecro vos]] [[1 Pet 2:11|to refrain yourselves from carnal desires which war against the soul|abstinere a carnalibus desideriis, quæ militant adversus animam]].

paras.t: Quod si spiritu ducimini, id est a Spiritu Sancto, non estis sub lege, id est, legalibus observantiis non subjicitis vosmetipsos. Tanquam dicat: In hoc constat vos esse deceptos, quod legis jugo subditi estis.
paras.en: [[5:18|But if you are led by the spirit|Quod si spiritu ducimini]], that is, by the Holy Ghost, [[5:18|you are not under the law|non estis sub lege]], that is, you do not subject yourselves to the legal observances. As if to say: In this it is plain that you have been deceived, that you are subject to the yoke of the law.

paras.t: Sciendum autem, quod spiritus multis modis accipitur in Scripturis: Primo, pro intellectuali et separata substantia: sicque Deus et angeli spiritus appellantur. Unde est illud: Spiritus est Deus; et in Actibus: Sadducæi dicunt, nec spiritum nec resurrectionem esse: ubi per spiritum angelus designatur. Secundo, pro substantia animæ, ut dum Stephanus ait: Domine, accipe spiritum meum. Tertio, pro superiori parte rationis, sicut hoc loco. Quarto, pro virtute imaginativa, ut ibi: Fui in spiritu in dominica die. Quinto, pro subtili humore per quem anima operationes vitales exercet in corpore, juxta illud: Spiritus diffundetur tanquam mollis aer. Sexto, pro aere vel vento, de quo quidam exponunt illud Geneseos: Spiritus Domini ferebatur super aquas; item et illud, Spiritus ubi vult spirat.
paras.en: Now it is to be known that *spirit* is taken in many ways in the Scriptures. First, for an intellectual and separate substance [that is, one not joined to a body]; and so God and the angels are called spirits. Hence that saying: [[John 4:24|God is a spirit|Spiritus est Deus]]; and in the Acts: [[Acts 23:8|the Sadducees say|Sadducæi dicunt]] that there is neither spirit nor resurrection; where by *spirit* an angel is meant. Secondly, for the substance of the soul, as when Stephen says: [[Acts 7:58|Lord|Domine]], [[Acts 7:58|receive my spirit|accipe spiritum meum]]. Thirdly, for the higher part of reason, as in this place. Fourthly, for the imaginative power, as there: [[Apoc 1:10|I was in the spirit on the Lord's day|Fui in spiritu in dominica die]]. Fifthly, for the subtle humour through which the soul exercises its vital operations in the body [the "spirits" of the old physiology], according to that: [[Wis 2:3|spirit shall be poured abroad as soft air|Spiritus diffundetur tanquam mollis aer]]. Sixthly, for air or wind, of which some expound that of Genesis: [[Gen 1:2|the spirit of God moved over the waters|Spiritus Domini ferebatur super aquas]] [Denis reads *Spiritus Domini*, "the spirit of the Lord"; the Vulgate has *Dei*]; and likewise that: [[John 3:8|The Spirit breatheth where he will|Spiritus ubi vult spirat]].

paras.t: Consequenter de operibus carnis quibus spiritus reluctatur, tractat Apostolus. Opera enim carnis proprie nominantur, ad quæ caro inclinat, ut sunt gula et luxuria, germinaque eorum. De quibus mox subditur: Manifesta autem sunt, id est, apertam malitiam habent, et naturali rationi opponuntur, opera carnis, quæ sunt, fornicatio, id est coitus soluti cum soluta, immunditia, id est vitium contra naturam, impudicitia, quantum ad gestus provocantes libidinem, in adspectu, tactu et osculis, luxuria, quæ est nomen commune quo cetera species luxuriæ jam non expressæ designantur, idolorum servitus, id est idololatria, quæ interdum ex luxuria generatur, ut patet in Salomone, veneficia, id est sortilegia, inimicitiæ, quæ ex carnali generantur amore, contentiones verborum, æmulationes, id est invidentiæ eorum qui idem appetunt, sed unus per alium impeditur, sicut dum plures ad præelationem adspirant, iræ, id est appetitus vindictæ, rixæ, id est lites verbosæ, dissensiones animorum, quantum ad partialitates, sectæ, id est separationes dissentientium jam firmatæ, invidiæ, homicidia, ebrietates, comessationes, id est assiduæ comestiones, et his similia, quæ prædico vobis vitanda, antequam morte præoccupemini, sicut prædixi: quoniam qui talia agunt, scilicet aliquod horum secundum suam perfectam rationem, regnum Dei non consequentur. Ex quo duo sequuntur: primum, quod omnia hæc sint peccata mortalia; alterum, quod damnati nunquam liberabuntur aut salvabuntur.
paras.en: Next the Apostle treats of the works of the flesh, against which the spirit struggles. For those things are properly called works of the flesh to which the flesh inclines, such as gluttony and lust, and their offshoots. Of these it is presently added: [[5:19|Now the works of the flesh|opera carnis]] [[5:19|are manifest|Manifesta autem sunt]], that is, they have open malice and are opposed to natural reason, [[5:19|which are|quæ sunt]] [[5:19|fornication|fornicatio]], that is, the intercourse of an unmarried man with an unmarried woman, [[5:19|uncleanness|immunditia]], that is, the vice against nature, [[5:19|immodesty|impudicitia]], as regards gestures that provoke lust, in looks, touches and kisses, [[5:19|luxury|luxuria]], which is a common name by which the other kinds of lust not already named are meant, [[5:20|idolatry|idolorum servitus]], which is sometimes born of lust, as is plain in Solomon[[3 Kings 11:1||]], [[5:20|witchcrafts|veneficia]], that is, sorceries, [[5:20|enmities|inimicitiæ]], which are born of carnal love, [[5:20|contentions|contentiones]] of words, [[5:20|emulations|æmulationes]], that is, the envyings of those who seek the same thing, but one is hindered by another, as when several aspire to a prelacy, [[5:20|wraths|iræ]], that is, the desire of revenge, [[5:20|quarrels|rixæ]], that is, wordy disputes, [[5:20|dissensions|dissensiones]] of minds, as regards factions, [[5:20|sects|sectæ]], that is, the separations of those who dissent, now hardened, [[5:21|Envies|invidiæ]], [[5:21|murders|homicidia]], [[5:21|drunkenness|ebrietates]], [[5:21|revellings|comessationes]], that is, constant eatings, [[5:21|and such like|et his similia]], [[5:21|Of the which I foretell you|quæ prædico vobis]] to be avoided, before you are overtaken by death, [[5:21|as I have foretold to you|sicut prædixi]], [[5:21|that they who do such things|quoniam qui talia agunt]], namely any one of these in its complete character [that is, fully, as a mortal sin], [[5:21|shall not obtain the kingdom of God|regnum Dei non consequentur]][[1 Cor 6:9||]][[1 Cor 6:10||]]. From which two things follow: first, that all these are mortal sins; second, that the damned will never be set free or saved.

paras.t: Insuper enumerantur opera Spiritus, id est, quæ a Spiritu Sancto in nobis fiunt, et spiritui nostro rationali insunt atque conveniunt. Dicuntur autem hæc opera, fructus, ad similitudinem fructus materialis. Sicut enim hujusmodi fructus ex terra aut arbore oritur, et cum quadam dulcedine degustatur, sic opera ista a Spiritu Sancto principaliter, atque a nostro spiritu divinitus confortato nascuntur, animamque delectant.
paras.en: Further, the works of the Spirit are listed, that is, those which are done in us by the Holy Ghost, and which are in our rational spirit and befit it. Now these works are called *fruit*, by likeness to material fruit. For as such fruit springs from the earth or from a tree, and is tasted with a certain sweetness, so these works spring from the Holy Ghost as their principal source, and from our spirit strengthened by God, and they delight the soul.

paras.t: Ait ergo: Fructus autem Spiritus Sancti seu nostri, est caritas, id est actus dilectionis, per modum ignis ad cœlestia scandens ac elevans, gaudium, id est diffusio animi in conceptione boni honesti: quod alio loco vocatur gaudium in Spiritu Sancto, nec competit reprobis. Est tamen et aliud gaudium, sæculare, vanum et falsum, de quo dicitur in Joanne: Mundus gaudebit; et in Job, Gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti. Pax, id est tranquillitas mentis seu quietatio ejus in bono, patientia in adversis, id est æquanimis perpessio contrariorum, longanimitas spei in præstolando bona divinitus promissa, bonitas, id est benevolentia, benignitas, id est benevolentiæ exsecutio, seu largitio facultatum, mansuetudo, id est tractabilitas iram repellens, fides, id est fidei certitudo sive fidelitas, modestia, id est moderatio in verbis et actibus, continentia, id est refrenatio voluptatis laboriosa, castitas, id est repressio venereorum et concupiscentiæ sine impugnatione atque labore. Continentia enim et castitas, quamvis circa idem versentur, nihilo minus tamen distinguuntur: quoniam continens sustinet concupiscentias fortes, sed non vincitur; castus vero nec sustinet eas, unde nec superatur.
paras.en: He says, then: [[5:22|But the fruit of the Spirit|Fructus autem Spiritus]], the Holy Spirit's or our own, [[5:22|is, charity|est caritas]], that is, the act of love, which like fire climbs to heavenly things and lifts up, [[5:22|joy|gaudium]], that is, the expanding of the mind on conceiving a good that is honest [that is, morally good in itself]: which in another place is called [[Rom 14:17|joy in the Holy Ghost|gaudium in Spiritu Sancto]] [the margin reads "Item xv, 17"; the words are Rom 14:17], and does not belong to the reprobate. There is, however, another joy too, worldly, vain and false, of which it is said in John: [[John 16:20|the world shall rejoice|Mundus gaudebit]]; and in Job, [[Job 20:5|the joy of the hypocrite but for a moment|Gaudium hypocritæ ad instar puncti]]. [[5:22|Peace|Pax]], that is, tranquillity of mind, or its rest in good, [[5:22|patience|patientia]] in adversity, that is, the even-minded enduring of contrary things, [[5:22|longanimity|longanimitas]] of hope in awaiting the good things promised by God, [[5:22|goodness|bonitas]], that is, benevolence [that is, the will to do good], [[5:22|benignity|benignitas]], that is, the carrying out of benevolence, or the bestowing of one's means, [[5:23|mildness|mansuetudo]], that is, a gentleness that repels anger, [[5:23|faith|fides]], that is, the certainty of faith, or fidelity, [[5:23|modesty|modestia]], that is, moderation in words and acts, [[5:23|continency|continentia]], that is, the laborious restraint of pleasure, [[5:23|chastity|castitas]], that is, the repression of venereal things and of concupiscence without assault and labour. For continence and chastity, though they are concerned with the same thing, are nevertheless distinguished: since the continent man suffers strong concupiscences but is not overcome; the chaste man does not even suffer them, and so is not overcome.

paras.t: Denique horum duodecim fructuum Spiritus, ad quos alii fructus reducuntur, distinctionem ac sufficientiam S. Thomas in prima secundæ ponit hoc modo: Fructus distinguuntur secundum varium processum Spiritus Sancti in nobis. Primo enim mens ordinatur in se ipsa per amorem, qui est radix omnium affectionum. Ideo primus fructus est caritas, sine qua nihil rationem fructus sortitur, et in qua Spiritus Sanctus specialiter datur. Secundo ponitur gaudium, quod ex caritate producitur: quoniam amans habendo amatum in se, gaudet de ejus præsentia, quam efficit caritas, juxta illud Evangelistæ: Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo. Tertius fructus est pax, quæ est perfectio gaudii: primo, propter quietem ab exteriori perturbatione: aliter namque non esset gaudium perfectum; secundo, propter interioris ac fluctuantis desiderii sedationem. Unde per hæc tria bene se habet anima in bonis. In malis quoque bene se habet dupliciter: primo, ne ex imminenti malo turbetur, quod fit per patientiam, quæ est quartus fructus; secundo, ne ex dilatione boni sperati frangatur, quod fit per longanimitatem, quæ est quintus fructus. — Secundo, bene disponitur homo ad id quod est juxta se, scilicet ad suum proximum: primo, per voluntatem benefaciendi, quod pertinet ad bonitatem, quæ est sextus fructus; secundo, per voluntatis istius exsecutionem, quod fit per benignitatem, quæ est septimus fructus; tertio, æquanimiter tolerando mala illata, quod fit per mansuetudinem, quæ est fructus octavus; quarto, ne proximis fraude aut dolo noceamus, quod fit per fidem pro fidelitate acceptam; si vero fides sumatur pro certitudine fidei, quæ est virtus theologica, sic per eam bene disponitur homo ad id quod supra se est, hoc est ad Deum, subdendo ei proprium intellectum. — Tertio, insuper recte disponitur ad id quod infra se est: primo, quantum ad verba et actus, quod est per modestiam, quæ ponitur decimus fructus; secundo, quantum ad interiorem passionem seu concupiscentiam: et ita ponuntur alii duo fructus, videlicet continentia et castitas, quorum differentia posita est.
paras.en: Lastly, St. Thomas, in the First Part of the Second Part [of the *Summa*], sets out the distinction and sufficiency of these twelve fruits of the Spirit, to which the other fruits are reduced, in this way: The fruits are distinguished according to the various ways in which the Holy Ghost proceeds in us. For first the mind is set in order within itself by love, which is the root of all the affections. Therefore the first fruit is charity, without which nothing has the character of fruit, and in which the Holy Ghost is especially given. Second is placed joy, which is produced by charity: since the lover, having the beloved in himself, rejoices in his presence, which charity brings about, according to that of the Evangelist: [[1 John 4:16|he that abideth in charity abideth in God, and God in him|Qui manet in caritate, in Deo manet, et Deus in eo]]. The third fruit is peace, which is the perfection of joy: first, because of rest from outward disturbance, for otherwise the joy would not be perfect; secondly, because of the stilling of inward and wavering desire. Hence through these three the soul is well disposed in good things. In evil things also it is well disposed in two ways: first, that it be not troubled by impending evil, which is done by patience, which is the fourth fruit; secondly, that it be not broken by the delay of the good hoped for, which is done by longanimity, which is the fifth fruit. — Secondly, man is well disposed towards what is beside him, namely his neighbour: first, by the will to do good, which belongs to goodness, which is the sixth fruit; secondly, by the carrying out of that will, which is done by benignity, which is the seventh fruit; thirdly, by bearing with even mind the evils done to him, which is done by mildness, which is the eighth fruit; fourthly, that we harm not our neighbours by fraud or guile, which is done by faith taken for fidelity; but if faith is taken for the certainty of faith, which is a theological virtue, then by it man is well disposed towards what is above him, that is, towards God, subjecting his own intellect to him. — Thirdly, moreover, he is rightly disposed towards what is beneath him: first, as to words and acts, which is through modesty, which is set as the tenth fruit; secondly, as to inward passion or concupiscence: and so the other two fruits are set down, namely continence and chastity, whose difference has been given.

paras.t: Quoniam vero juxta præhabita, fructus nominat operationem, caritas, patientia, mansuetudo, etc., prout fructus ponuntur, non accipiuntur pro ipsis habitibus, sed habituum actibus. Sciendum quoque, quod fructus vocantur, non solum actus virtutum delectabiles, sed etiam delectationes actibus virtuosis annexæ. Idcirco prædicta omnia accipi possunt tam pro actibus virtuosis, quam pro delectationibus mundis. Iterum advertendum, quod virtutes et dona conveniunt in hoc quod sunt habitus; sed virtutes perficiunt potentias animæ, dona vero perficiunt ipsas virtutes. Simili modo beatitudines et fructus conveniunt in hoc quod sunt actus virtutum seu donorum; sed beatitudo superaddit ad rationem fructus excellentiam quamdam. Beatitudines namque sunt actus præcipuarum excellentiumque virtutum: propter quod potius attribuuntur donis quam virtutibus. Omnes ergo beatitudines fructus dici possunt, non autem econtrario.
paras.en: But since, according to what has been said, *fruit* names an operation, charity, patience, mildness, etc., as they are set down as fruits, are not taken for the habits themselves, but for the acts of the habits. It is to be known also that not only the delightful acts of the virtues are called fruits, but also the delights joined to virtuous acts. Therefore all the foregoing may be taken both for virtuous acts and for pure delights. Again it is to be noted that the virtues and the gifts [that is, the seven gifts of the Holy Ghost] agree in this, that they are habits; but the virtues perfect the powers of the soul, while the gifts perfect the virtues themselves. In like manner the beatitudes and the fruits agree in this, that they are acts of the virtues or of the gifts; but beatitude adds to the notion of fruit a certain excellence. For the beatitudes are acts of the chief and most excellent virtues: for which reason they are attributed to the gifts rather than to the virtues. All the beatitudes, therefore, can be called fruits, but not the other way round.

paras.t: Adversus hujusmodi fructus Spiritus non est lex prohibens eos, sed pro eis est lex.
paras.en: [[5:23|Against such|Adversus hujusmodi]] fruits of the Spirit [[5:23|there is no law|non est lex]] forbidding them; rather, the law is for them.

paras.t: Qui autem sunt Christi per fidem et caritatem perfectam, id est imitatores Crucifixi, carnem suam crucifixerunt, id est, spiritualiter mortificaverunt, eam macerando, affligendo, domando, cum vitiis exterioribus, et concupiscentiis interioribus, tam vitia quam concupiscentias persequendo et occidendo.
paras.en: [[5:24|And they that are Christ's|Qui autem sunt Christi]] by faith and perfect charity, that is, the imitators of the Crucified, [[5:24|have crucified their flesh|carnem suam crucifixerunt]], that is, have mortified it spiritually, by macerating, afflicting and taming it, [[5:24|with the vices|cum vitiis]] without [[5:24|and concupiscences|et concupiscentiis]] within, pursuing and slaying both vices and concupiscences.

paras.t: Consequenter Apostolus exhortationem convertit ad Galatas. Si, pro quia, spiritu, id est rationis judicio vel Spiritus Sancti operatione, vivimus intra nos vita gratiæ, spiritu et ambulemus, id est, rationis judicium seu Spiritus Sancti instinctum sequamur in conversatione exteriori et vita aliis exemplari, ut luceat lux nostra coram hominibus, quatenus videntes opera nostra bona, ædificentur, et Deum glorificent.
paras.en: Next the Apostle turns his exhortation to the Galatians. [[5:25|If|Si]], put for *since*, [[5:25|in the Spirit|spiritu]], that is, by the judgment of reason or by the working of the Holy Ghost, [[5:25|we live|vivimus]] within ourselves the life of grace, [[5:25|let us also walk in the Spirit|spiritu et ambulemus]], that is, let us follow the judgment of reason or the prompting of the Holy Ghost in our outward conduct and in a life that is an example to others, so that our light may shine before men, that seeing our good works they may be edified and glorify God[[Matt 5:16||]].

paras.t: Verumtamen, ne in hoc aliquo modo propriam gloriam intendamus, subjungitur: Non efficiamur inanis gloriæ cupidi, id est, non appetamus ab hominibus æstimari aut honorari, invicem provocantes verbis vel signis, invicem invidentes. Invidia enim quum directe adversetur caritati, quæ est animæ vita, maxime perhibetur mors esse animæ. Hinc est illud Joannis: Qui non diligit, manet in morte: omnis qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est. Propterea dicit Salvator: In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem.
paras.en: But lest in this we should in any way seek our own glory, he adds: [[5:26|Let us not be made desirous of vain glory|Non efficiamur inanis gloriæ cupidi]], that is, let us not desire to be esteemed or honoured by men, [[5:26|provoking one another|invicem provocantes]] by words or signs, [[5:26|envying one another|invicem invidentes]]. For since envy is directly opposed to charity, which is the life of the soul, it is said to be above all the death of the soul. Hence that saying of John: [[1 John 3:14|He that loveth not abideth in death|Qui non diligit, manet in morte]]: [[1 John 3:15|Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer|omnis qui odit fratrem suum, homicida est]]. Therefore the Saviour says: [[John 13:35|By this shall all men know that you are my disciples, if you have love one for another.|In hoc cognoscent omnes quia discipuli mei estis, si dilectionem habueritis ad invicem]].

6.title: EXPOSITIO CAPITULI SEXTI : FRATRES, ETSI PRÆOCCUPATUS FUERIT HOMO IN ALIQUO DELICTO.
6.title_en: Exposition of the sixth chapter: Brethren, and if a man be overtaken in any fault.

paras.t: Hortatur demum Apostolus in hujus capituli exordio prælatos et perfectiores, ut imperfectis ac subditis pie condescendant atque subveniant. Ait enim:
paras.en: Lastly, at the beginning of this chapter, the Apostle exhorts prelates and the more perfect to condescend kindly to the imperfect and to those under them, and to come to their help. For he says:

paras.t: Fratres, etsi præoccupatus, id est, quamvis præventus seu comprehensus, fuerit homo ex subito motu passionis, infirmitate, seu ignorantia, in aliquo delicto ex hujusmodi causa exorto: vos qui spirituales estis, id est virtutibus exercitati, hujusmodi hominem instruite, id est, ad viam veritatis reducite, atque corrigite, in spiritu lenitatis, id est animo mansueto ac dulci, non impetuoso aut graviter indignanti, considerans te ipsum, id est, propriæ conditionis fragilitatem attendens, ne et tu tenteris, id est, simili modo delinquas: hoc est, estote aliis misericordes et compatientes, ut et vos misericordiam consequamini, si culpam inciderit. Etenim beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur: et, Benefacit animæ suæ homo misericors. Propterea quoque et alibi dicitur: Memento judicii mei: sic enim erit et tuum. Mihi heri, et tibi hodie. Mutat autem hoc loco Apostolus numerum, sicut frequenter fit in Scripturis.
paras.en: [[6:1|Brethren, and if a man be overtaken|Fratres, etsi præoccupatus]], that is, although [[6:1|a man|fuerit homo]] be forestalled or caught, through a sudden motion of passion, through weakness or through ignorance, [[6:1|in any fault|in aliquo delicto]] arising from a cause of this kind, [[6:1|you, who are spiritual|vos qui spirituales estis]], that is, practised in the virtues, [[6:1|instruct such a one|hujusmodi hominem instruite]], that is, lead him back to the way of truth and correct him, [[6:1|in the spirit of meekness|in spiritu lenitatis]], that is, with a gentle and sweet mind, not impetuous or gravely indignant, [[6:1|considering thyself|considerans te ipsum]], that is, attending to the frailty of thy own condition, [[6:1|lest thou also be tempted|ne et tu tenteris]], that is, lest thou also sin in like manner. That is to say: be merciful and compassionate to others, that you too may obtain mercy if one of you should fall into fault. For [[Matt 5:7|Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy|beati misericordes, quoniam ipsi misericordiam consequentur]]; and, [[Prov 11:17|A merciful man doth good to his own soul|Benefacit animæ suæ homo misericors]]. For this reason it is also said elsewhere: [[Ecclus 38:23|Remember my judgment: for thine also shall be so: yesterday for me, and to day for thee|Memento judicii mei: sic enim erit et tuum. Mihi heri, et tibi hodie]] [the margin gives Eccli. xxxviii, 24; in the Vulgate the verse is Ecclus 38:23]. Now in this place the Apostle changes the number [from *you who are spiritual* to *considering thyself*], as often happens in the Scriptures.

paras.t: Alter alterius onera portate, id est, defectus vestros et infirmitates atque peccata mutuo patienter sufferte, orando pro alterutro, mutuo succurrendo verbis ac rebus. Unde et alibi ait: Supportantes invicem in caritate. Hoc verbo redarguuntur complures, qui in aliorum defectibus mox inflammantur, et rigide quasi sub specie justitiæ afficiuntur; propria vero vitia non corrigunt, neque ab aliis dure increpari dignantur. Et sic adimplebitis legem Christi, id est caritatis præceptum, de quo ait Christus: Mandatum novum do vobis: ut diligatis invicem, sicut dilexi vos. Hæc itaque agite, et nolite in delicto præoccupatum dure corripere, quamvis ex deliberatione seu certa malitia peccans, sit dure corripiendus.
paras.en: [[6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]], that is, bear patiently with one another's defects, weaknesses and sins, praying for one another and helping one another by words and deeds. Whence he says elsewhere too: [[Eph 4:2|supporting one another in charity|Supportantes invicem in caritate]]. By this word many are rebuked who are quickly inflamed at the defects of others and are rigidly moved against them, as if under the appearance of justice, yet do not correct their own vices, nor will they deign to be harshly rebuked by others. [[6:2|and so you shall fulfil the law of Christ|Et sic adimplebitis legem Christi]], that is, the precept of charity, of which Christ says: [[John 13:34|A new commandment I give unto you: That you love one another, as I have loved you|Mandatum novum do vobis: ut diligatis invicem, sicut dilexi vos]]. Do these things, therefore, and do not harshly rebuke one overtaken in a fault; though one who sins from deliberation or from certain malice [that is, knowingly and of set purpose, not from passion, weakness or ignorance] is to be rebuked harshly.

paras.t: Nam si quis existimat se aliquid esse a se ipso, vel spiritualiter, seu comparatione Sanctorum, quum nihil sit a se ipso, et quantum ad esse gratificum, spirituale ac meritorium, seu comparatione Sanctorum. Nam etsi aliquid esset per gratiam, tamen reputando se tumide, perdit quod habuit, juxta quod dicitur: Sola superbia destruit omnia, si committitur. Hinc ait Psalmista: Substantia mea tanquam nihilum ante te; item Ecclesiasticus. Quid superbit, inquit, terra et cinis? Ipse se seducit, id est, in falsitatem præcipitat, et damnationem incurrit.
paras.en: [[6:3|For if any man think himself to be some thing|Nam si quis existimat se aliquid esse]] of himself, either spiritually or in comparison with the Saints, [[6:3|whereas he is nothing|quum nihil sit]] of himself, both as to the being of grace [*esse gratificum*: the being that grace gives], spiritual and meritorious, and in comparison with the Saints. For even if he were something through grace, yet by esteeming himself with swollen pride he loses what he had, according to the saying: Pride alone destroys all things, if it is committed. Hence the Psalmist says: [[Ps 38:6|my substance is as nothing before thee|Substantia mea tanquam nihilum ante te]]; and Ecclesiasticus likewise: [[Ecclus 10:9|Why|Quid superbit]], he says, [[Ecclus 10:9|is earth, and ashes proud|terra et cinis]]? [[6:3|he deceiveth himself|Ipse se seducit]], that is, he casts himself headlong into falsehood and incurs damnation.

paras.t: Opus autem suum probet unusquisque, id est, totam vitam suam prudenter examinet, et sic in semetipso tantum gloriam habebit, id est, de propriis bonis seu conscientiæ suæ testimonio exsultabit, si fuerit virtuosus: non tamen finaliter aut principaliter in se, sed in Domino, juxta illud, Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Unde et dictum est: Gloria nostra hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ. Et non in altero, id est, de factis et meritis aliorum non præsumet, neque aliorum laude et adulatione lætabitur. Quis enim scit quid agatur in homine, nisi spiritus hominis?
paras.en: [[6:4|But let every one prove his own work|Opus autem suum probet unusquisque]], that is, let him prudently examine his whole life, [[6:4|and so he shall have glory in himself only|et sic in semetipso tantum gloriam habebit]], that is, he will exult in his own good things, or in the testimony of his conscience, if he has been virtuous; yet not finally or principally in himself, but in the Lord, according to that: [[1 Cor 1:31|He that glorieth may glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]]. Whence it has also been said: [[2 Cor 1:12|our glory is this: the testimony of our conscience|Gloria nostra hæc est, testimonium conscientiæ nostræ]]. [[6:4|and not in another|Et non in altero]], that is, he will not presume upon the deeds and merits of others, nor rejoice in the praise and flattery of others. For [[1 Cor 2:11|what man knoweth the things of a man, but the spirit of a man|Quis enim scit quid agatur in homine, nisi spiritus hominis?]] [Denis's wording: who knoweth what is done in a man, but the spirit of a man]?

paras.t: Unusquisque enim onus suum, id est causam quam cum districto judice habet expedire, seu conscientiæ suæ gravamen, vel vitiorum suorum ultionem, vel actionum suarum manipulum, portabit. Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos.
paras.en: [[6:5|For every one|Unusquisque enim]] [[6:5|shall bear|portabit]] [[6:5|his own burden|onus suum]], that is, the cause which he has to settle with the strict Judge, or the burden of his conscience, or the punishment of his vices, or the sheaf of his actions. [[Apoc 14:13|For their works follow them|Opera enim illorum sequuntur illos]].

paras.t: Porro prædicta jam verba Apostoli non secundum superficiem litteralem, sed sapienter intelligenda sunt. Alias enim invicem secum pugnarent. Dixit namque, Alter alterius onera portate; nunc vero adjunxit, Unusquisque onus suum portabit, quasi unus non sit portaturus onus alterius. Item alibi dicit, Nemo glorietur in hominibus; et, Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur. Nunc autem testatus est. In semetipso tantum gloriam habebit. Sed si sane intelligantur, et modus ac ordo atque intentio quibus introducuntur, pensentur, nulla erit discordia.
paras.en: Further, these words of the Apostle just quoted are to be understood not according to their literal surface, but wisely; otherwise they would fight with one another. For he said, [[6:2|Bear ye one another's burdens|Alter alterius onera portate]]; and now he has added, [[6:5|every one shall bear his own burden|Unusquisque onus suum portabit]], as though one were not to bear the burden of another. Again, elsewhere he says, [[1 Cor 3:21|Let no man therefore glory in men|Nemo glorietur in hominibus]]; and, [[1 Cor 1:31|He that glorieth may glory in the Lord|Qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur]] [the margin reference here is unreadable; the same words stand also at 2 Cor 10:17]. But now he has declared: [[6:4|he shall have glory in himself only|In semetipso tantum gloriam habebit]]. But if they are soundly understood, and the manner, order and intention with which they are brought in are weighed, there will be no discord.

paras.t: Communicet autem, id est, se conformet, vel subveniat, is qui catechizatur, id est instruitur, verbo sapientiæ salutaris, ei qui se catechizat, id est suo instructori, in omnibus bonis operibus, non autem in vitiis; vel, In omnibus bonis, id est divitiis seu facultatibus, ut ei in temporalibus administret a quo spiritualia bona suscipit.
paras.en: [[6:6|And let him that is instructed|is qui catechizatur]], that is, taught, [[6:6|in the word|verbo]] of saving wisdom, [[6:6|communicate|Communicet autem]], that is, conform himself or give help, [[6:6|to him that instructeth him|ei qui se catechizat]], that is, to his instructor, [[6:6|in all good things|in omnibus bonis operibus]]: in good works, that is, but not in vices; or, in all good things, that is, riches or means, so that he may minister in temporal things to him from whom he receives spiritual goods.
