paras.t: Nolite errare a luce veritatis et via justitiæ, excusando vos a prædicta communicatione, vel aliorum præceptorum exsecutione. Deus non irridetur, id est, non fallitur: ideo scit an excusatio sit condigna et verax.
paras.en: [[6:7|Be not deceived|Nolite errare]] [*errare* is also "to stray"], straying from the light of truth and the way of justice by excusing yourselves from the communicating just spoken of, or from carrying out the other precepts. [[6:7|God is not mocked|Deus non irridetur]], that is, he is not deceived; and so he knows whether the excuse be worthy and true.

paras.t: Quod autem Deus non irrideatur, hinc constat: Quæ enim seminaverit homo, id est opera quæ in hac vita effecerit, quæ ad futura præmia comparantur sicut semen ad fructum; hæc et metet, id est, horum fructum seu mercedem recipiet, juxta illud: Anima ejus in vita ipsius benedicetur; item et illud, Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique juxta opera sua.
paras.en: That God is not mocked is plain from this: [[6:8|For what things a man shall sow|Quæ enim seminaverit homo]], that is, the works he has done in this life, which are compared to the rewards to come as seed to fruit, [[6:8|those also shall he reap|hæc et metet]], that is, he shall receive their fruit or reward; according to that: [[Ps 48:19|in his lifetime his soul will be blessed|Anima ejus in vita ipsius benedicetur]]; and also that: [[Apoc 22:12|Behold, I come quickly: and my reward is with me, to render to every, man according to his works|Ecce venio cito, et merces mea mecum est, dare unicuique juxta opera sua]].

paras.t: Quoniam qui seminat in carne sua, id est, carnaliter vivit, impetum passionum sequendo, de carne, id est pro vitiis carnis, et metet, id est recipiet, corruptionem peccati ac mortis æternæ. Qui autem seminat in spiritu, id est, spiritualiter conversatur, rationis sententiam et caritatis instinctum semper sequendo, de spiritu, id est pro operibus spiritualibus, vel de Spiritu Sancto tanquam a remuneratore, metet vitam æternam, id est, cœlestem beatitudinem consequetur in præmium.
paras.en: [[6:8|For he that soweth in his flesh|Quoniam qui seminat in carne sua]], that is, lives carnally, following the impulse of the passions, [[6:8|of the flesh|de carne]], that is, for the vices of the flesh, [[6:8|also shall reap|et metet]], that is, shall receive, [[6:8|corruption|corruptionem]] of sin and of everlasting death. [[6:8|But he that soweth in the spirit|Qui autem seminat in spiritu]], that is, lives spiritually, always following the verdict of reason and the prompting of charity, [[6:8|of the spirit|de spiritu]], that is, for spiritual works, or of the Holy Ghost as the one who rewards, [[6:8|shall reap life everlasting|metet vitam æternam]], that is, shall obtain heavenly beatitude as his reward.

paras.t: Bonum autem, id est opus virtutis, facientes, non deficiamus, id est, nequaquam cessemus, nec tepescamus. Non enim coronatur, nisi qui legitime certaverit; et, Qui perseveraverit in finem, salvus erit. Tempore enim suo, id est hora divinæ retributionis, videlicet quum ab omni culpa et pœna fuerimus absoluti, sive in hac vita, sive in purgatorio, metemus, id est, æternam gloriam recipiemus, non deficientes, id est, finem non habituri præmii tanti, nec plus appetituri quam dabitur.
paras.en: [[6:9|And in doing good|Bonum autem]], that is, the work of virtue, [[6:9|let us not fail|non deficiamus]], that is, let us by no means cease or grow lukewarm. For he [[2 Tim 2:5|is not crowned, except he strive lawfully|Non enim coronatur, nisi qui legitime certaverit]] [the margin gives 1 Tim. ii, 5; the passage is 2 Tim 2:5]; and, [[Matt 10:22|he that shall persevere unto the end, he shall be saved|Qui perseveraverit in finem, salvus erit]][[Matt 24:13||]]. [[6:9|For in due time|Tempore enim suo]], that is, at the hour of the divine repayment, namely when we have been loosed from all guilt and punishment, whether in this life or in purgatory, [[6:9|we shall reap|metemus]], that is, we shall receive eternal glory, [[6:9|not failing|non deficientes]], that is, never to have an end of so great a reward, nor to desire more than will be given.

paras.t: Ergo dum tempus promerendi habemus, id est, quamdiu durat vita hæc præsens, operemur bonum ad omnes, id est, omnibus quantum possibile est, benefaciamus, sicut generalis exigit caritas, corporalia seu spiritualia bona nostra eis communicando. Maxime autem operemur bonum ad domesticos fidei, id est Ecclesiæ filios, veros Christianos, quibus alibi dicit Apostolus: Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei. Qui ergo nobis magis conjuncti sunt, his magis benefacere obligamur. Caritas namque est ordinata. Propter quod rursus alibi ait Apostolus: Si quis, inquiens, suorum, et maxime domesticorum, curam non habet, fidem negavit, et est infideli deterior.
paras.en: [[6:10|Therefore, whilst we have time|Ergo dum tempus promerendi habemus]] for meriting, that is, as long as this present life lasts, [[6:10|let us work good to all men|operemur bonum ad omnes]], that is, let us do good to all as far as is possible, as charity towards all requires, sharing with them our goods of body or of soul. [[6:10|but especially|Maxime autem]] let us work good [[6:10|to those who are of the household of the faith|ad domesticos fidei]], that is, to the sons of the Church, true Christians, to whom the Apostle says elsewhere: [[Eph 2:19|you are no more strangers and foreigners: but you are fellow citizens with the saints and the domestics of God|Jam non estis hospites et advenæ, sed estis cives Sanctorum et domestici Dei]]. Those, then, who are more closely joined to us, we are the more bound to do good to; for charity is ordered [that is, it loves in due order, the nearer first]. For this reason the Apostle says again elsewhere: [[1 Tim 5:8|if any man|Si quis]], he says, [[1 Tim 5:8|have not care of his own and especially of those of his house, he hath denied the faith and is worse than an infidel|suorum, et maxime domesticorum, curam non habet, fidem negavit, et est infideli deterior]].

paras.t: Videte qualibus litteris scripsi vobis mea manu, id est, considerate quali sermone ego præsentem epistolam dictavi, et manu propria scripsi, ne quis vos decipiat, dicendo epistolam hanc non esse missam a me, vel simili stilo vobis scribendo.
paras.en: [[6:11|See what a letter I have written to you with my own hand|Videte qualibus litteris scripsi vobis mea manu]], that is, consider in what words I have dictated the present letter and written it with my own hand, lest anyone deceive you by saying that this letter was not sent by me, or by writing to you in a like style.

paras.t: Quicumque enim volunt placere sibi ipsis in carne vestra, id est præputii vestri circumcisione; vel, qui volunt placere Judæis incredulis in carne, id est in carnalibus observantiis, hi cogunt, id est, vehementer et importune quærunt et excitant, vos circumcidi in corpore, tantum, id est præsertim ad hoc, ut persecutionem crucis Christi, id est persecutionem pro fide et passione Salvatoris, non patiantur a Judæis: qui eos persequebantur qui cessationem legalium docuerunt. Pseudo enim apostoli legalia simul cum Evangelio prædicaverunt, ne a Judæis infidelibus paterentur molestias.
paras.en: [[6:12|For as many as desire to please|Quicumque enim volunt placere]] themselves [[6:12|in the flesh|sibi ipsis in carne vestra]] [Denis reads *placere sibi ipsis in carne vestra*, "to please themselves in your flesh"], that is, in the circumcision of your foreskin; or, who wish to please the unbelieving Jews in the flesh, that is, in carnal observances, [[6:12|they constrain|hi cogunt]], that is, vehemently and importunately seek and urge, [[6:12|you to be circumcised|vos circumcidi]] in the body, [[6:12|only|tantum]], that is, chiefly to this end, [[6:12|that they may not suffer|non patiantur]] [[6:12|the persecution of the cross of Christ|ut persecutionem crucis Christi]], that is, persecution for the faith and passion of the Saviour, from the Jews, who persecuted those who taught that the legal observances had ceased. For the false apostles preached the legal observances together with the Gospel[[Acts 15:1||]][[Acts 15:2||]], so as not to suffer trouble from the unbelieving Jews.

paras.t: Neque enim qui circumciduntur carnaliter, legem custodiunt spiritualiter, neque præceptis legis moralibus vere obtemperant; sed volunt vos circumcidi, ut in carne vestra, id est de vestri circumcisione carnali, glorientur inaniter, quasi voluntatis suæ effectum in vobis adepti.
paras.en: [[6:13|For neither they themselves who are circumcised|Neque enim qui circumciduntur]] in the flesh [[6:13|keep the law|legem custodiunt]] spiritually, nor do they truly obey the moral precepts of the law; [[6:13|but they will have you to be circumcised|sed volunt vos circumcidi]], [[6:13|that they may glory|glorientur]] vainly [[6:13|in your flesh|ut in carne vestra]], that is, in your carnal circumcision, as though they had obtained in you the effect of their own will.

paras.t: Mihi autem absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini nostri Jesu Christi, id est in contemplatione Filii Dei crucifixi, et beneficiorum ipsius, videlicet in consideratione passionis, caritatis, et obedientiæ Christi. Per hoc tamen non excluditur gloriatio in divinitate et excellentia Salvatoris, quoniam gloriatio crucis ordinatur ad illam sicut ad ultimum finem. Unde et illa datur in ista intelligenda. Absit itaque a me gloriari in circumcisione, in cærimonialibus legis, in rebus caducis et vanis; sed hæc sit gloriatio mea, in Christi passione occupari, ejus beneficia meditari, ipsius vestigia sequi. Per quem Christum, id est per cujus gratiam, passionem et imitationem, mihi mundus crucifixus est, id est mortuus, utputa, tam homines sæculares, quam concupiscentiæ atque divitiæ sæculi hujus, ita ut talia mihi non sapiant, non delectent, non vivant, nec me sibi conjungant inordinato affectu; et ego mundo per Christum crucifixus, id est mortuus, sum, ita ut mundo non placeam, non vivam, neque communicem, juxta illud: Quoniam propter te mortificamur tota die.
paras.en: [[6:14|But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ|Mihi autem absit gloriari, nisi in cruce Domini nostri Jesu Christi]], that is, in the contemplation of the Son of God crucified and of his benefits, namely in the consideration of the passion, the charity and the obedience of Christ. Yet by this, glorying in the Godhead and excellence of the Saviour is not excluded, since the glorying of the cross is ordered to that as to its last end; and so that glorying is given to be understood in this one. Far be it from me, then, to glory in circumcision, in the ceremonies of the law, in perishable and vain things; but let this be my glorying: to be busied with the passion of Christ, to meditate on his benefits, to follow in his footsteps. [[6:14|by whom|Per quem]] Christ, that is, through whose grace, passion and imitation, [[6:14|the world is crucified to me|mihi mundus crucifixus est]], that is, dead: both worldly men, for instance, and the desires and riches of this world, so that such things have no savour for me, give me no delight, have no life for me, and do not join me to themselves with disordered affection; [[6:14|and I to the world|et ego mundo]] am crucified through Christ, that is, dead, so that I do not please the world, nor live to it, nor share with it; according to that: [[Ps 43:22|Because for thy sake we are killed all the day long|Quoniam propter te mortificamur tota die]] [the margin gives Ps. xliv, 22, the Hebrew numbering; in the Vulgate it is Ps 43:22].

paras.t: Denique absit mihi gloriari, nisi in cruce Christi: In Christo enim Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet ad veram salutem, neque præputium, id est ritus gentilitatis, sed nova creatura, id est spiritualis regeneratio ex aqua et Spiritu, seu vita recens per gratiæ quotidianam innovationem.
paras.en: Finally, [[6:14|God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross|absit mihi gloriari, nisi in cruce]] of Christ: [[6:15|For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision availeth any thing|In Christo enim Jesu neque circumcisio aliquid valet]] for true salvation, [[6:15|nor uncircumcision|neque præputium]], that is, the rite of the Gentiles, [[6:15|but a new creature|sed nova creatura]], that is, spiritual regeneration [[John 3:5|of water and the Holy Ghost|ex aqua et Spiritu]], or a life made new by the daily renewal of grace.

paras.t: Et quicumque hanc regulam, id est gloriationis hujus rectitudinem atque mensuram, secuti fuerint, pax interna, id est tranquillitas cordis, sit super illos et misericordia, id est peccatorum remissio, et super Israel Dei, id est, super electos Judæos, legalia successive deserentes, et fidem catholicam amplectentes, sit pax ista et misericordia.
paras.en: [[6:16|And whosoever|Et quicumque]] [[6:16|shall follow|secuti fuerint]] [[6:16|this rule|hanc regulam]], that is, the rightness and measure of this glorying, inward [[6:16|peace|pax interna]], that is, tranquillity of heart, be [[6:16|on them and mercy|super illos et misericordia]], that is, the remission of sins; [[6:16|and upon the Israel of God|et super Israel Dei]], that is, upon the chosen Jews, who were leaving the legal observances by degrees and embracing the Catholic faith, may this peace and mercy be.

paras.t: De cetero nemo mihi molestus sit, dicendo, aut mihi imponendo observationem legalium, vel ad delectamenta præsentis vitæ me exhortando. Ego enim stigmata Domini Jesu, id est signa vulnerum et similitudinem pœnarum Christi, in corpore meo porto, bajulando crucem meam indesinenter, et Christum sequendo, ejusque passioni me pro viribus conformando.
paras.en: [[6:17|From henceforth let no man be troublesome to me|De cetero nemo mihi molestus sit]] by urging upon me, or laying upon me, the observance of the legal rites, or by exhorting me to the delights of the present life. [[6:17|for I bear the marks of the Lord Jesus|Ego enim stigmata Domini Jesu]], that is, the signs of the wounds and the likeness of the sufferings of Christ, [[6:17|in my body|in corpore meo porto]], carrying my cross unceasingly[[Luke 14:27||]] and following Christ[[Luke 9:23||]], and conforming myself to his passion as far as my strength allows.

paras.t: Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro, id est in anima vestra, o fratres. Amen. Hæc est gratia gratum faciens, quæ a tota Trinitate infunditur, quamvis interim etiam unicuique divinæ Personæ attribuatur. Tota enim superbeatissima Trinitas inseparabiliter operatur ad extra: quæ est super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: [[6:18|The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit|Gratia Domini nostri Jesu Christi sit cum spiritu vestro]], that is, in your soul, [[6:18|brethren. Amen|o fratres. Amen]]. This is sanctifying grace [*gratia gratum faciens*, the grace that makes one pleasing to God], which is poured in by the whole Trinity, although it is also at times attributed to each divine Person. For the whole most supremely blessed Trinity works inseparably *ad extra* [that is, in its works outside the Godhead]: the Trinity which is God above all, exalted and blessed. Amen.
